Add inspect_il2cpp_metadata (CLI inspect-il2cpp-metadata), a read-only

overlapping sections, inconsistent record sizes, out-of-range indices and

A 112,232-method file produced a 10.5 MB complete response, above the
10 MiB stdio budget. Default MCP delivery is now the retained summary;
detail complete stays available, and the one-shot CLI requests it.

* fix(il2cpp): reject shifted strings, nesting cycles and method owner drift

Review fuzzing showed that moving the strings section offset by one byte
silently renamed every image, type and method. Name indices must now start
a string, which also bounds total decoding by the section size.

Nesting cycles and methods whose declaring type disagrees with the owning
type range are rejected instead of returned. Adds service, shutdown and
index-width coverage, and moves environment-specific measurements out of
the public guide and tool description.

* feat(il2cpp): decode global-metadata versions 29 and 31

Unity 2022.3 writes version 29 or 31 metadata: a 256-byte header of
(offset, size) pairs, fixed 4-byte indices, type records with
elementTypeIndex, and method records that gained returnParameterToken in
version 31. Record counts come from section sizes and must be whole.

Sections report a null count for these versions and index widths report
fixed-width-version. Image, type and method rows keep the same shape, and
the string, nesting and method-ownership checks apply to every version.

* fix(il2cpp): bound report size before serializing and tighten coverage

Rows share decoded names, so a 130 KB file could expand into gigabytes of
JSON before the 64 MiB budget check, ending in an internal RangeError. The
provider now refuses from a lower bound on the serialized rows first.

The decoder also rejects non-empty sections inside the header, methods
outside their declaring type's range and overlapping image type ranges, and
keeps a leading byte order mark in names. Layouts now carry one indexing
mode instead of two coupled flags, and the tool description explains
nested_type_start.

* fix(il2cpp): refuse oversized metadata before decoding rows

Address review findings on the IL2CPP metadata inventory:

- check a lower bound from header row counts before any row object is
  allocated, so a large rejected file no longer builds every row first;
- validate sealed parent Evidence and count its rows once per report
  instead of on every inspect_analysis_view page;
- decode version 39 fixtures with 2- and 4-byte type-definition,
  generic-container and parameter indices.

* docs(il2cpp): attach the decoder comment to readIl2cppMetadata

* fix(il2cpp): deliver complete rows by default like the other inspection tools

inspect_il2cpp_metadata defaulted to detail summary, the only inspection
tool to do so. Omitted detail now returns every row inline, as
inspect_artifact, decode_interface_builder and the capture tools do;
summary stays one argument away and the guide, CLI reference and skill
reference say to select it first for large games, whose complete MCP
delivery is refused at the stdio budget with retained Evidence.

* test(il2cpp): cover narrow-width -1 sentinels and fix the skill's default

An empty image stores its type start as the all-ones value of a one- or
two-byte index; the decoder reads it as -1, but no fixture exercised it,
so removing either conversion passed the suite. The fixture can now append
an empty image, and both widths decode it. The skill still described a
summary default; it now says to select summary first, as the guide does.

* docs(il2cpp): request summary explicitly in the summary example

* chore(il2cpp): hash the verifier metadata through owned file resources

* fix(il2cpp): count escaped name length without building the escaped string

* fix(il2cpp): keep the verifier's check failure and small-table last page

* feat(domain): count JSON string length without building the escaped string

* fix(il2cpp): keep descriptor cleanup owners and share the JSON length count

* test(domain): give the backslash case real backslashes

* fix(il2cpp): select the CLI path and finish the command like the other tools

Follow main's absoluteCallerPath (#4067) and pass the command signal to finishAnalysisCommand.

* fix(il2cpp): select the verifier input path like the CLI

Use absoluteCallerPath (#4067) so a path with a symlink followed by .. names the same file the CLI and MCP inspect.

* feat(il2cpp): add compact composable metadata queries

Retain source-indexed Evidence for filtered batch and field queries. Bound representation growth before serialization, yield decoding for cancellation, and share CLI Evidence publication with desktop inspection. Verify public Unity metadata against independent byte and managed-DLL oracles and exercise actual stdio SDK workflows.

* fix(il2cpp): retain the validated metadata header magic

* test(il2cpp): remove obsolete execution wording exception

* fix(artifacts): preserve export selection and completed source facts

commits.subject: feat(environment): extract the initial state a capture's reads observed (#5319)
commits.body:
feat(environment): extract the initial state a capture's reads observed (#5319)

* feat(environment): extract the initial state a capture's reads observed

Add the environment-state analysis view. From the parents the environment
manifest accepts, it extracts the data the capture's reads observed before
the first related write: entity types with an identity field (proved by a
path parameter or inferred from an identity name), entities with their
recorded values and provenance, documents for written non-entity paths, and
a render plan per read tool that is kept only when it reproduces the tool's
latest initial recordings from the state; every other read tool is a
recorded view with the reason. The Evidence is always inferred.

Response-body decoding moves to a domain owner shared with replay, exact
JSON parsing moves to the owner of the exact-number policy, the manifest and
state views share parent admission and record grouping, and
projectAnalysisView takes its accumulators as one object.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(environment): bound state at redacted writes; infer identity only from items

A scenario write whose URL was redacted has no request line, so it was
dropped and reads after it counted as initial state. Such a successful
write now joins the timeline with an empty path, whose root relates to
every type, so it ends every type's state; a limitation counts them.

A list whose recordings were all empty passed the "every listed item
carries it" check vacuously and published an identity field nothing
showed; it now needs at least one item, else the view stays recorded
as no-identity.

A value that differed between two request lines of one item tool, such
as a query variant, was called volatile, and the gate then substituted
each recording's own value; only repeats of one request line now show
volatility, so differing lines go through fields-differ.

List membership is compared only while a list can still be the whole
collection, and merged entities are indexed by type and collection once,
so paged captures no longer cost pages times entities (8,000 pages of
40,000 entities: 5.7 s to 0.23 s).

Docs and the tool contract say scenario state keeps the capture's
redaction markers and how redacted writes bound it.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(environment): keep first sightings, one list pointer and linear field unions

Entities took the order of the first plan observed, and item plans run
before list plans, so a complete list read before its detail reads came
out reordered and lost "all" membership; each entity now keeps its
earliest recorded sighting.

A list plan reused the first recording's pointer for later recordings,
so a later response that was itself an entity wrapping a list was read
as that list; every recording must now locate the same list.

The field union scanned its ordered list for every key, quadratic in an
object's width; a set now answers membership.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(environment): keep post-write values and partial lists out of the initial state

A value that changed between repeats of one request line was named
volatile whenever no write under the type's own root lay between, so a
write under another root (for example POST /api/dashboards/db before a
second GET /api/search) left its effect in the initial state. Any
recorded write between the two observations now leaves every tool of the
type recorded with reason fields-differ instead.

A list was published with membership "all" even when a total or count
envelope member exceeded the number it listed. Such a counter now makes
the membership "recorded".

Also drop a stale doc comment on ObservedEntity.order.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* docs(environment): scope item-shaped and deleted written paths out of documents

State documents are held only for list-shaped paths a POST, PUT or PATCH
tool writes. Reads of item-shaped written paths and of paths that are only
deleted stay recorded views; the guide now says so and the spec defers them
to a later increment of #4933.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(environment): count writes in flight when a value changes between reads

The volatility check compared write start positions with the two reads,
so a write already in flight when the earlier read started was missed and
its effect was named volatile. A write now counts when its interval
overlaps the span from the earlier read's start to the later read's end.

The check also ran once per changed field and scanned every write. It now
runs once per pair of observations, answered by a binary search over the
writes in timeline order and the latest end among each prefix.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(environment): catch cross-tool changes across writes; read only item totals

A value that changed across a write was caught only between repeats of
one tool's request line, so a list read before a write and an item read
after it put the post-write value into the initial state. Changes are
now classified per entity in timeline order after observation: across
any recorded write, a change between repeats of a line or between two
lines of the type rewrites the type (every tool recorded as
fields-differ); with no write between, a repeat's change is volatile.
The classification lives in environmentStateMerge.ts.

Any numeric member whose name contained "total" or "count" counted as
an item total, so total_pages, account_id or page_count made complete
lists partial. Item totals are now members whose name tokens include
total or count and none of page, pages or per; a string of digits counts
as a number; and a set has_more, next or next-page token member also
marks the list partial.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(environment): keep post-write observations out of initial state

* fix(environment): retain field provenance and bound state inference work

* ci: split fast and deep static checks

Fast PRs run typecheck, lint, and format before provider admission.

* ci: keep pull requests from writing the remote cache

Trusted default-branch runs still receive TURBO_TOKEN. Pull requests get an
empty token and remote read-only mode. Knip saves a per-commit cache key so
the next trusted full run can refresh the restored snapshot.

Co-authored-by: morluto <morluto@users.noreply.github.com>

* ci: forward the release cache token and upload deep static reports

Release qualification now passes TURBO_TOKEN into the called workflow.

context and uploads duplication reports after a failed gate.

implementations. Lock check:ci:fast around dist, and publish the remote cache
only for release qualification or default-branch push, schedule, and dispatch.

Co-authored-by: morluto <morluto@users.noreply.github.com>

* ci: record static task graphs without nesting the artifacts lock

Keep check:ci:fast locked, and point graph recording at the unlocked
check:ci:fast:tasks script so check:pr and check:test can record hashes
while they already hold that lock.

authenticate. Those runs now use the local cache. Trusted runs still publish.

Reuse identical LC_LAZY_LOAD_DYLIB_INFO ranges, cap their combined size,
and reject flag or chain-start offsets outside the slice VM range.

Co-authored-by: morluto <morluto@users.noreply.github.com>

* fix(apple): bound lazy-load string scans and contained reads

Reject payload strings that start in the 24-byte header, validate each
file-offset string once, and reuse payload bytes already read for a
containing range.

Co-authored-by: morluto <morluto@users.noreply.github.com>

Remember each cached string's terminating offset and require that NUL to
fall inside the payload being decoded.

Count containment checks across earlier payload reads and stop at the
existing 16 MiB work limit.

* fix(apple): count every lazy-info string reference

Charge repeated and overlapping LC_LAZY_LOAD_DYLIB_INFO scans against the
16 MiB validation budget, and stop a scan once that budget is exhausted.

Co-authored-by: morluto <morluto@users.noreply.github.com>

* fix(apple): cap retained lazy-info dependency results

Stop after 1024 LC_LAZY_LOAD_DYLIB_INFO commands so a load-command region
full of identical commands cannot become a million traced edges.

dyld stops the load-path scan before the payload's last byte, so a
terminator in that byte leaves the image malformed.

commits.body:
fix(errors): name fixed allowances in resource-constraint recovery (#5633)

* fix(errors): name fixed allowances in resource-constraint recovery

Fixed parser, count, report, input, and capture refusals inherited
host-memory, wait-and-retry, or retained-Evidence advice. Producers now
attach allowance-specific recovery, and deterministic capacity caps are
not retryable. IL2CPP reader occupancy stays retryable capacity.

Refs #5556, #5405, #5456, #5459, #5460, #5504, #5505, #5506, #5537, #5628, #5630, #5631, #5632

* fix(il2cpp): keep a closing metadata reader non-retryable

close() stops admission before the active inspection finishes. A second
inspect in that window was projected as retryable capacity. Closing and
closed readers now report capability_unavailable. Occupied readers that
remain open stay retryable.

* fix(errors): align fixed-cap recovery with retained facts

IL2CPP report refusals keep observed source facts instead of denying Evidence. Command-output caps use the capture allowance. Ghidra seed recovery names the limit that was exceeded.

* fix(errors): call byte caps a byte allowance

WASM representation limits and the IL2CPP Ghidra seed-file cap are byte budgets. Their recovery no longer says the exceeded allowance is a fixed count.

* test(ida): keep unresolved procedure lookups non-retryable

Main now treats an unchanged invalid request as non-retryable. The IDA lookup tests follow that projection.

* fix(errors): qualify capture recovery for live output

A fixed capture allowance still rejects the same output. Live captures such as adb logcat can change between requests, so recovery no longer says every unchanged request fails again.

* fix(adb): keep a truncated live capture retryable

Device output can shrink between calls, so an adb capture that exceeds the allowance stays retryable. Deterministic capture and version-output limits stay non-retryable.

* fix(adb): keep truncated mutations non-retryable

Only live observations opt into retrying a capture that exceeded the allowance. Push, install, uninstall, and other mutations stay non-retryable.

* fix(errors): keep live capture recovery off deterministic limits

Artifact-derived capture allowances again say the unchanged request fails. Only volatile adb observations use the live-output sentence.

commits.body:
fix(process): token-check identityless exit-refresh replacements (#5675)

* fix(process): token-check identityless exit-refresh replacements

A launcher-exit refresh could drop a reparented grandchild that was absent
from the prior snapshot and report cleanup complete, or publish a verified
empty lineage, without reading its run token.

Fixes #5206

Co-authored-by: morluto <morluto@users.noreply.github.com>

* fix(process): re-read identityless refresh rows when relations change

Lineage refresh classified every pre-existing process as a newcomer, and it
skipped a row after caching its first parent and group. Seed the exclusion
set from the initial snapshot and read a row again when that relation changes.

Co-authored-by: morluto <morluto@users.noreply.github.com>

* style: format files oxfmt rejects on main

Repo-wide format:check fails on these two files at current main. Align them
so the process-ownership fix can pass the required static check.

Co-authored-by: morluto <morluto@users.noreply.github.com>

* fix(process): keep owned groups found while confirming exit

An unreadable exit-refresh row used to hide the confirmation table, and
revalidation dropped groups discovered after the plan was built. Both now
stay in the same cleanup, and confirmation reads are bounded.

Co-authored-by: morluto <morluto@users.noreply.github.com>

* fix(process): reclassify lineage rows when tree membership changes

Initial outsiders and cached refresh rows are read again when a parent,
group, or ancestor move changes launcher-tree membership. Unchanged
initial rows stay unread.

Co-authored-by: morluto <morluto@users.noreply.github.com>

* fix(process): re-read cached identityless lineage tokens

Parent and group do not identify a process generation. A row whose token
was read is read again on the next refresh, so a reused PID cannot keep
a verified descendant.

Co-authored-by: morluto <morluto@users.noreply.github.com>

* fix(process): revalidate an owned group that reappears

A group discovered after it was already processed is queued once more.
Another appearance stays unresolved instead of reporting cleanup complete.

Co-authored-by: morluto <morluto@users.noreply.github.com>

* fix(process): recheck a helper that changes groups during confirmation

The confirmation table can move a token-matched member into a new group.
That row is read again, and cleanup signals the group it belongs to now.

Co-authored-by: morluto <morluto@users.noreply.github.com>

* fix(process): publish one lineage row when a descendant returns

A refreshed descendant replaces the initial row for the same PID, including
when its group moves away and then returns to the original relation.

Co-authored-by: morluto <morluto@users.noreply.github.com>

* fix(process): re-read foreign PIDs on the exit confirmation table

A readable foreign token does not identify a process that later reuses
that PID. The confirmation table reads those newcomers again.

Co-authored-by: morluto <morluto@users.noreply.github.com>

* fix(process): recheck a pre-exit PID whose relation changes

An unchanged pre-existing row stays unread. A prior PID whose parent or
group changed is token-checked, so a reused owned process is not skipped.

Co-authored-by: morluto <morluto@users.noreply.github.com>

* fix(process): recheck an initial descendant after its token matches

A successful read in the first lineage pass marks that PID token-checked.
A later refresh reads it again, so a reused PID cannot stay verified.

Co-authored-by: morluto <morluto@users.noreply.github.com>

* fix(process): recheck the launcher on each lineage refresh

A later refresh reads the launcher PID again. A missing or unowned
launcher is unavailable instead of rooting a verified lineage.

Co-authored-by: morluto <morluto@users.noreply.github.com>

* fix(process): publish lineage from the latest refresh table

A descendant missing from the latest refresh is omitted. A refreshed
launcher whose group or command no longer matches stays unavailable.

Co-authored-by: morluto <morluto@users.noreply.github.com>

* test(process): cover a refreshed launcher parent mismatch

A same-token launcher whose parent no longer matches the committed
expected parent is unavailable, same as a group or command change.

Co-authored-by: morluto <morluto@users.noreply.github.com>

* fix(process): recheck a token-read helper that returns to its group

A confirmation table dropped a previously matched PID once its parent and
group matched the pre-exit row, so cleanup could signal only the group it
had joined and report success while that helper survived.

commits.body:
fix(windows): retain native handles when close is unconfirmed (#5772)

* fix(windows): retain native handles whose close is unconfirmed

CloseHandle failure no longer drops the numeric value. A still-open handle
stays owned and can be closed again; a value missing from the handle table
is dropped and never closed again; unreadable liveness blocks another close
until a probe says the value is open.

Co-authored-by: morluto <morluto@users.noreply.github.com>

* test(process): keep scratch until inherited pipes close

Lock the execFileOutput settlement contract: an inherited-pipe descendant
holds the caller's scratch root until it exits, and destroying the readers
is not process-family completion.

Co-authored-by: morluto <morluto@users.noreply.github.com>

* fix(windows): retry admitted file closes before runtime removal

A failed private-file close stays on the runtime that opened it. Runtime
removal closes that same wrapper before the tree walk, including when the
read that opened the file has already returned.

Co-authored-by: morluto <morluto@users.noreply.github.com>

* fix(windows): resume a close after part of the owner is released

A runtime whose directory handle is already released continues with its
parent handles instead of walking that invalid root. A process whose
settlement was already observed retries process close alone, without kill
or poll against the released job.

Co-authored-by: morluto <morluto@users.noreply.github.com>

* test(process): signal only an owned inherited-pipe descendant

Skip the descendant SIGKILL after pipe settlement. On an earlier failure,
signal only when the process command line still contains that test's path.

Co-authored-by: morluto <morluto@users.noreply.github.com>

* fix(windows): do not close a handle again after a failed close

An open liveness probe can observe a reused numeric value. After CloseHandle
fails, drop the value only when the handle table no longer contains it, and
do not call CloseHandle on that number again.

Co-authored-by: morluto <morluto@users.noreply.github.com>

* fix(windows): stop using a close-blocked pipe for I/O

A broken pipe whose CloseHandle fails stays owned, but its numeric value
may have been reused. Later polls and stdin writes treat that pipe as
ended instead of reading or writing the number.

commits.subject: fix(apple): keep scalar facts when object-table entries share a record (#5806)
commits.body:
fix(apple): keep scalar facts when object-table entries share a record (#5806)

Binary plist object tables may list one object offset more than once;
plistlib reads each entry independently. The scalar scanner marked any
repeated offset as incomplete metadata, which made the number projection
drop every exact decimal in the archive. A keyed archive whose entries
10 and 11 share an Int64 9007199254740993 reported both as observed
9007199254740992 and rounded an unrelated 2^60+3 sibling, with only the
generic incomplete-metadata caveat.

A repeated valid offset carries the same source facts as its first
visit, so observe it once and continue. Offsets that fail to parse still
mark metadata incomplete. Shared 16-byte integers and dates are rewritten
once in the decoder copy, which every entry then reads; the overlap plan
already treats one shared offset as one span. Keyed archives and
Interface Builder decoding share this scanner.

commits.subject: feat(analysis-view): share templated positions across manifest tools (#5664)
commits.body:
feat(analysis-view): share templated positions across manifest tools (#5664)

* docs(specs): plan a template rule that shares templated positions

Record the outcome, requirements, non-goals, plan and tasks for
prefix-variance, an opt-in environment-manifest rule that templates a
literal segment with the parameter another tool already uses at that
position, so a session's writes to one entity share the read's template.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(analysis-view): share templated positions across manifest tools

Add the opt-in prefix-variance template rule. It runs after the other
opt-in rules and templates a literal at a position that another tool,
of any method or segment count, templates by one of those rules after
the same preceding parts, when the literal is one of that parameter's
observed values or carries a digit and is spelled like one. The
parameter takes the shared parameter's name, tools that now match merge,
and a merged position keeps a tool's own rule when one templated it.

A write to the one entity a session edited, such as
PATCH /api/v1/collections/0RZ576QZQA5KG, becomes
patch_collections_by_collection_id on the read's template instead of a
literal single-entity tool.

Tool naming moves to its own module, and the three comparing passes
share the 32-segment split. Manifests that do not list the rule are
unchanged.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* refactor(analysis-view): drop the unused ManifestRule alias

Parameters now type their rule as a format rule, a shared opt-in rule
or prefix-variance, so nothing reads the union alias.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* docs(specs): record the prefix-variance checks and corpus results

Record the gates, and the 50 showcase captures with and without the
rule: identical output without it, 25 write and 34 read tools templated
with it, and the write tools the write-plan branch serves on top.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(analysis-view): share positions with digit-free generated identifiers

prefix-variance accepted an unobserved literal only when it carried a
digit, so a generated identifier that happened to hold none stayed a
literal tool: an n8n workflow id such as FkMwxmXNGaGVsXFG, whose reads
then never joined the item view. A literal now also qualifies when every
value observed at the position has one length of eight or more characters
and the literal has that length and uses only their character classes.

Across the 50 showcase captures this templates 10 more read tools in
Memos and n8n and no words.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* docs(specs): record five environments rebuilt end to end with the rule

Five randomly drawn environments rebuilt on VMs with the rule and the
write-plan branch: smoke, retrieval and write tasks for two models, and
the same calls against the live applications. Record the results, the
misses and their causes, and the corpus numbers after the fixed-length
clause.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(analysis-view): share a position with the parameter that observed the literal

A shared position folded every donor's values into the earliest donor's
parameter. With an opaque-token read before sibling-variance reads at
the same position, a PATCH of /api/items/b2 qualified on the sibling's
evidence but became /api/items/{uid} instead of joining the item read's
/api/items/{item_id}. Each position now keeps one donor per naming rule
with its own values, and a literal takes the donor that observed it,
else the earliest one it is spelled like.

Each donor's spelling (length and character classes of its values, and
its fixed-length family) is summarised once per position, so a literal
is checked in time independent of how many values were observed, rather
than copying and rescanning them for every candidate.

A family now forms from one observed value, as the requirement says, so
a digit-free id of the same length shares a position that only one
opaque-token or after-uid-literal tool supplied. The 50 showcase
captures give the same tools as before.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* docs(specs): record the prefix-variance review round

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(analysis-view): bound the spelling summary of shared positions

spellingSummary classified every observed value with three full-size
replaceAll copies and a set per distinct character, so a donor holding
a multi-megabyte segment cost unaccounted memory and time in finish().
Characters are now classified in one pass, and a value longer than 128
characters takes no part in spelling comparisons: it shares a position
only as an exactly observed value. The 50 showcase captures give the
same tools.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Co-authored-by: morluto <morluto@users.noreply.github.com>

A failed close used to be retained and then ignored, so MCP could return

retry that removed the stage could not clear the error, so

retained resource after cleanup had completed.

failure, to its exact leases so confirmed release restores the primary

commits.body:
fix(javascript): count one IPC observation per site-resolved channel (#5810)

* fix(javascript): count one IPC observation per site-resolved channel

A send with a local constant channel was recorded twice: once unresolved
by the syntax pass and once resolved by wrapper substitution, because
duplicates were keyed on the channel. A channel the call site determines
now resolves that observation in place. A channel supplied through a
wrapper argument stays a candidate beside the unresolved observation.
Invocation identity now follows the call that supplies the wrapper's
literal arguments, so one wrapper call reached through several entries
is recorded once.

Fixes #5710

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(javascript): keep wrapper invocations distinct while removing repeats

Taking the nearest literal call as invocation identity collapsed separate
outer calls that pass different handlers through one wrapper call. Entry
identity is restored, and a finding is a repeat only when an identical
finding was reached through the same trailing local calls. A registration
replaces its unresolved source observation only when the site also
determines its handler, so a parameter handler keeps the generic source
registration beside per-invocation candidates.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(javascript): compare site-determined IPC handlers by value

In-place resolution compared handler representations, so a constant
channel with a named local handler (recorded as an identifier by the
syntax pass and as its function by substitution) stayed counted twice.
The handler is now site-determined when it evaluates to the same function
in the site's lexical environment. A replaced observation also removes
the syntax pass's unknown-channel contribution, so a fully resolved file
is no longer reported as partial.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(javascript): keep closures over invocation values as distinct IPC handlers

A handler node created in different wrapper activations may capture
different values, so the same function node alone does not prove the call
site determines the registration.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* test(javascript): guard optional call paths in closure handler test

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(javascript): decide IPC handler identity from activation captures

A closure is one site-determined handler only when it reads no binding of a
function this trace activated, such as a wrapper parameter or factory local.
Unused bindings in the activation no longer split a known listener, and
closures over outer-call values stay distinct when a shorter entry traced
the same wrapper call.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(javascript): treat implicit captures and bundle modules precisely in IPC handler identity

An arrow handler reading its enclosing function's arguments or this captures
that activation. A bundle module factory runs once per module load, so its
bindings are shared by every trace rather than per-invocation captures.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: feat(environment)!: serve the environment state by default (#5351)
commits.body:
feat(environment)!: serve the environment state by default (#5351)

* feat(environment): extract the initial state a capture's reads observed

Add the environment-state analysis view. From the parents the environment
manifest accepts, it extracts the data the capture's reads observed before
the first related write: entity types with an identity field (proved by a
path parameter or inferred from an identity name), entities with their
recorded values and provenance, documents for written non-entity paths, and
a render plan per read tool that is kept only when it reproduces the tool's
latest initial recordings from the state; every other read tool is a
recorded view with the reason. The Evidence is always inferred.

Response-body decoding moves to a domain owner shared with replay, exact
JSON parsing moves to the owner of the exact-number policy, the manifest and
state views share parent admission and record grouping, and
projectAnalysisView takes its accumulators as one object.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(environment): bound state at redacted writes; infer identity only from items

A scenario write whose URL was redacted has no request line, so it was
dropped and reads after it counted as initial state. Such a successful
write now joins the timeline with an empty path, whose root relates to
every type, so it ends every type's state; a limitation counts them.

A list whose recordings were all empty passed the "every listed item
carries it" check vacuously and published an identity field nothing
showed; it now needs at least one item, else the view stays recorded
as no-identity.

A value that differed between two request lines of one item tool, such
as a query variant, was called volatile, and the gate then substituted
each recording's own value; only repeats of one request line now show
volatility, so differing lines go through fields-differ.

List membership is compared only while a list can still be the whole
collection, and merged entities are indexed by type and collection once,
so paged captures no longer cost pages times entities (8,000 pages of
40,000 entities: 5.7 s to 0.23 s).

Docs and the tool contract say scenario state keeps the capture's
redaction markers and how redacted writes bound it.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(environment): keep first sightings, one list pointer and linear field unions

Entities took the order of the first plan observed, and item plans run
before list plans, so a complete list read before its detail reads came
out reordered and lost "all" membership; each entity now keeps its
earliest recorded sighting.

A list plan reused the first recording's pointer for later recordings,
so a later response that was itself an entity wrapping a list was read
as that list; every recording must now locate the same list.

The field union scanned its ordered list for every key, quadratic in an
object's width; a set now answers membership.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(environment): keep post-write values and partial lists out of the initial state

A value that changed between repeats of one request line was named
volatile whenever no write under the type's own root lay between, so a
write under another root (for example POST /api/dashboards/db before a
second GET /api/search) left its effect in the initial state. Any
recorded write between the two observations now leaves every tool of the
type recorded with reason fields-differ instead.

A list was published with membership "all" even when a total or count
envelope member exceeded the number it listed. Such a counter now makes
the membership "recorded".

Also drop a stale doc comment on ObservedEntity.order.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* docs(environment): scope item-shaped and deleted written paths out of documents

State documents are held only for list-shaped paths a POST, PUT or PATCH
tool writes. Reads of item-shaped written paths and of paths that are only
deleted stay recorded views; the guide now says so and the spec defers them
to a later increment of #4933.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(environment): count writes in flight when a value changes between reads

The volatility check compared write start positions with the two reads,
so a write already in flight when the earlier read started was missed and
its effect was named volatile. A write now counts when its interval
overlaps the span from the earlier read's start to the later read's end.

The check also ran once per changed field and scanned every write. It now
runs once per pair of observations, answered by a binary search over the
writes in timeline order and the latest end among each prefix.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(environment): catch cross-tool changes across writes; read only item totals

A value that changed across a write was caught only between repeats of
one tool's request line, so a list read before a write and an item read
after it put the post-write value into the initial state. Changes are
now classified per entity in timeline order after observation: across
any recorded write, a change between repeats of a line or between two
lines of the type rewrites the type (every tool recorded as
fields-differ); with no write between, a repeat's change is volatile.
The classification lives in environmentStateMerge.ts.

Any numeric member whose name contained "total" or "count" counted as
an item total, so total_pages, account_id or page_count made complete
lists partial. Item totals are now members whose name tokens include
total or count and none of page, pages or per; a string of digits counts
as a number; and a set has_more, next or next-page token member also
marks the list partial.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(environment): keep post-write observations out of initial state

* fix(environment): retain field provenance and bound state inference work

* feat(environment): serve tool calls from the environment state

`environment-serve --state <state.json>` serves an environment from the
initial state an environment-state view extracted. Read tools whose views
are state-backed answer from a live state store: item views render the held
entity into the recorded envelope, list views render the collection or the
recorded members, and document views return the held value; a missing entity
or one lacking a required field is refused, and requests the state cannot
answer fall back to their recordings with the reason. The /agentenv data
plane implements data/reset, data/add (a rea-state/v1 document as a data
part, base64 bytes, a file:// path or an https URL, validated and replaced
atomically) and data/get, and the card advertises those operations and an
intake declaration. Stage 1 is read-only: write tools are not served in
state mode. Without --state nothing changes.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* docs(environment): record verification after merging the state view's review fixes

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(environment)!: serve the environment state by default

environment-serve derives the environment state at startup by running the
environment-state view in-process on the capture with the manifest's
template rules, so an environment comes with its state and a user supplies
nothing extra. The derived Evidence is the same one inspect-analysis-view
produces by hand. --state is removed; --replay-only serves exactly the
stateless replay of main. When the state cannot be derived, or its catalog
does not fit the discovery budget, the server starts in replay mode, logs
the reason and reports it in the stop summary's `state`. Exported bundles
serve the state by default too: export derives it the same way, so the
verifier's tool count and checked answer match what is served, and the
README describes the served mode.

BREAKING CHANGE: environment-serve answers read tools from the derived
state and does not serve write tools unless --replay-only is given; the
stop summary reports `state` instead of `state_evidence_id`.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(environment): bound data-plane replies, keep batch order, cancel intake on stop

- One /agentenv response is held to 64 MiB: replies are measured as they
  are produced and one past the budget becomes a -32000 error stating it.
- Every message of a batch enters the arrival-order queue on arrival, so
  another request's reset never lands between them.
- Stopping the server, or a caller leaving, cancels the active download
  and answers queued calls `cancelled` without running them.
- file:// URIs name only this host: another host or a network share is
  refused before anything is opened.
- A loaded view value may not give an entity another identity.
- List answers refuse a member lacking a field every recording carried,
  as item answers do.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(environment): keep bodies too deep for the state's nesting out of the state

A recorded body at the JSON depth limit was accepted by extraction, then
nested a few levels deeper as a document or entity value, so sealing the
state Evidence threw and environment-serve and environment-export stopped
instead of falling back. stateBodyJson, the one rule extraction and
serving share, now treats a body nesting deeper than the limit minus 16
levels as unusable, so its tool stays a recorded view.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(environment): measure data-plane replies before building them

83fcc739 bounded one /agentenv response to 64 MiB, but it still
serialized each reply whole before measuring it, so a batch of data/get
calls on a large state built every refused reply in full only to drop
it. Each reply is now measured in bounded JSON parts (the shared
jsonParts encoder), its parts kept only while it fits; a reply past the
budget is counted for its exact reply_bytes but never assembled. A test
checks that a refused read is never handed to JSON.stringify whole and
that its reply_bytes is exact.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(environment): release batch replies as they are encoded; judge exact numbers by value

answerBatch kept every settled reply in its pending array until the
batch ended, so a batch alternating data/add and data/get held each
loaded state alive; each reply now leaves the queue as it is encoded.

The exact-number policy judged a number by its recorded spelling, so a
state loaded with 1e20 came back from data/get as
100000000000000000000, which data/add refused, breaking the promise
that data/get output loads back unchanged. A number is exact only when
both its recorded spelling and the one serialization writes are safe,
so integers from 2^53 below 1e21 are refused in any spelling; replay
keeps such bodies as recorded text. A domain test checks that every
accepted number is accepted again once written back.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(environment): keep room for refusals and framing in the reply budget

The response budget counted accepted replies only: a budget error that
replaced a reply, and a batch's brackets and commas, were not charged,
so near 64 MiB later refusals pushed the body past the advertised
limit. Every reply still to come now keeps room for its own budget
error, and a batch keeps room for its framing, so a refusal always fits
and the body never passes the budget. Reply ids and which messages are
answered come from one place shared by the replies and the reserve.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(environment): refuse a loaded state that data/get would write past the intake limit

data/add measured only the document it was given, while data/get
writes the state back with the members a document may omit (types, the
state Evidence id, view fields and record citations). A document just
under 32 MiB could therefore load and be reported larger than any intake
accepts, breaking the data/get then data/add round trip. replace now
measures the state as data/get writes it, part by part, and refuses it
past the limit, leaving the state unchanged. The limit moves to the
state document module, so the application store can read it; the
intake re-exports it.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(environment): keep merged export checks on the shared test graph

Main's export tests installed module mocks for the whole services
project, which reuses one module graph. A tarball read failure then
missed its importer, and a one-shot heap mock could be taken by another
file. Read those through bindings the tests replace for one case.

Co-authored-by: morluto <morluto@users.noreply.github.com>

* fix(environment): keep a state file whose close failed owned until it closes

A file:// data/add that could not close its descriptor dropped the handle,
and an admission failure whose cleanup close failed dropped its owner, so
nothing could retry the close or report it.

The read now runs through withOwnedRegularFile, and a failed close is
retained in a server-lifetime ArtifactResourceScope. The next file read
retries it first and answers -32000 while it is still open; inline and
https documents still load. Closing the served environment retries it again
and rejects with the unfinished close.

* fix(browser): name web-bundle budgets and recover web deadlines

Name the existing heap, per-script, and total web-bundle phases, and reject a per-script deadline above the total. Promote capture, CDP command, source-map decode, and source-map fetch deadlines at today's defaults. Name DevTools timeoutMs, and state that discovery, cleanup grace, byte budgets, and Electron hook retention have no runtime override.

* fix(browser): apply selected web deadlines to the owning phase

Keep HTTP and browser-socket discovery on the fixed discovery deadline so a
short command_timeout_ms starts at the handshake. Apply scenario
command_timeout_ms to launch startup and the primary connect session, and
keep service-worker restoration on the fixed 5000 ms grace. Omit
command_timeout_ms from recovery text when the operation does not accept it.

browser or context and restore a mutation that lands after the deadline.

implements beginCleanupGrace.

* fix(browser): keep child command timeouts as the public failure

commits.subject: fix(environment): bound state reads and retain cleanup ownership (#6158)
commits.body:
fix(environment): bound state reads and retain cleanup ownership (#6158)

* feat(environment): extract the initial state a capture's reads observed

Add the environment-state analysis view. From the parents the environment
manifest accepts, it extracts the data the capture's reads observed before
the first related write: entity types with an identity field (proved by a
path parameter or inferred from an identity name), entities with their
recorded values and provenance, documents for written non-entity paths, and
a render plan per read tool that is kept only when it reproduces the tool's
latest initial recordings from the state; every other read tool is a
recorded view with the reason. The Evidence is always inferred.

Response-body decoding moves to a domain owner shared with replay, exact
JSON parsing moves to the owner of the exact-number policy, the manifest and
state views share parent admission and record grouping, and
projectAnalysisView takes its accumulators as one object.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(environment): bound state at redacted writes; infer identity only from items

A scenario write whose URL was redacted has no request line, so it was
dropped and reads after it counted as initial state. Such a successful
write now joins the timeline with an empty path, whose root relates to
every type, so it ends every type's state; a limitation counts them.

A list whose recordings were all empty passed the "every listed item
carries it" check vacuously and published an identity field nothing
showed; it now needs at least one item, else the view stays recorded
as no-identity.

A value that differed between two request lines of one item tool, such
as a query variant, was called volatile, and the gate then substituted
each recording's own value; only repeats of one request line now show
volatility, so differing lines go through fields-differ.

List membership is compared only while a list can still be the whole
collection, and merged entities are indexed by type and collection once,
so paged captures no longer cost pages times entities (8,000 pages of
40,000 entities: 5.7 s to 0.23 s).

Docs and the tool contract say scenario state keeps the capture's
redaction markers and how redacted writes bound it.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(environment): keep first sightings, one list pointer and linear field unions

Entities took the order of the first plan observed, and item plans run
before list plans, so a complete list read before its detail reads came
out reordered and lost "all" membership; each entity now keeps its
earliest recorded sighting.

A list plan reused the first recording's pointer for later recordings,
so a later response that was itself an entity wrapping a list was read
as that list; every recording must now locate the same list.

The field union scanned its ordered list for every key, quadratic in an
object's width; a set now answers membership.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(environment): keep post-write values and partial lists out of the initial state

A value that changed between repeats of one request line was named
volatile whenever no write under the type's own root lay between, so a
write under another root (for example POST /api/dashboards/db before a
second GET /api/search) left its effect in the initial state. Any
recorded write between the two observations now leaves every tool of the
type recorded with reason fields-differ instead.

A list was published with membership "all" even when a total or count
envelope member exceeded the number it listed. Such a counter now makes
the membership "recorded".

Also drop a stale doc comment on ObservedEntity.order.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* docs(environment): scope item-shaped and deleted written paths out of documents

State documents are held only for list-shaped paths a POST, PUT or PATCH
tool writes. Reads of item-shaped written paths and of paths that are only
deleted stay recorded views; the guide now says so and the spec defers them
to a later increment of #4933.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(environment): count writes in flight when a value changes between reads

The volatility check compared write start positions with the two reads,
so a write already in flight when the earlier read started was missed and
its effect was named volatile. A write now counts when its interval
overlaps the span from the earlier read's start to the later read's end.

The check also ran once per changed field and scanned every write. It now
runs once per pair of observations, answered by a binary search over the
writes in timeline order and the latest end among each prefix.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(environment): catch cross-tool changes across writes; read only item totals

A value that changed across a write was caught only between repeats of
one tool's request line, so a list read before a write and an item read
after it put the post-write value into the initial state. Changes are
now classified per entity in timeline order after observation: across
any recorded write, a change between repeats of a line or between two
lines of the type rewrites the type (every tool recorded as
fields-differ); with no write between, a repeat's change is volatile.
The classification lives in environmentStateMerge.ts.

Any numeric member whose name contained "total" or "count" counted as
an item total, so total_pages, account_id or page_count made complete
lists partial. Item totals are now members whose name tokens include
total or count and none of page, pages or per; a string of digits counts
as a number; and a set has_more, next or next-page token member also
marks the list partial.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(environment): keep post-write observations out of initial state

* fix(environment): retain field provenance and bound state inference work

* feat(environment): serve tool calls from the environment state

`environment-serve --state <state.json>` serves an environment from the
initial state an environment-state view extracted. Read tools whose views
are state-backed answer from a live state store: item views render the held
entity into the recorded envelope, list views render the collection or the
recorded members, and document views return the held value; a missing entity
or one lacking a required field is refused, and requests the state cannot
answer fall back to their recordings with the reason. The /agentenv data
plane implements data/reset, data/add (a rea-state/v1 document as a data
part, base64 bytes, a file:// path or an https URL, validated and replaced
atomically) and data/get, and the card advertises those operations and an
intake declaration. Stage 1 is read-only: write tools are not served in
state mode. Without --state nothing changes.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* docs(environment): record verification after merging the state view's review fixes

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(environment)!: serve the environment state by default

environment-serve derives the environment state at startup by running the
environment-state view in-process on the capture with the manifest's
template rules, so an environment comes with its state and a user supplies
nothing extra. The derived Evidence is the same one inspect-analysis-view
produces by hand. --state is removed; --replay-only serves exactly the
stateless replay of main. When the state cannot be derived, or its catalog
does not fit the discovery budget, the server starts in replay mode, logs
the reason and reports it in the stop summary's `state`. Exported bundles
serve the state by default too: export derives it the same way, so the
verifier's tool count and checked answer match what is served, and the
README describes the served mode.

BREAKING CHANGE: environment-serve answers read tools from the derived
state and does not serve write tools unless --replay-only is given; the
stop summary reports `state` instead of `state_evidence_id`.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(environment): bound data-plane replies, keep batch order, cancel intake on stop

- One /agentenv response is held to 64 MiB: replies are measured as they
  are produced and one past the budget becomes a -32000 error stating it.
- Every message of a batch enters the arrival-order queue on arrival, so
  another request's reset never lands between them.
- Stopping the server, or a caller leaving, cancels the active download
  and answers queued calls `cancelled` without running them.
- file:// URIs name only this host: another host or a network share is
  refused before anything is opened.
- A loaded view value may not give an entity another identity.
- List answers refuse a member lacking a field every recording carried,
  as item answers do.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(environment): keep bodies too deep for the state's nesting out of the state

A recorded body at the JSON depth limit was accepted by extraction, then
nested a few levels deeper as a document or entity value, so sealing the
state Evidence threw and environment-serve and environment-export stopped
instead of falling back. stateBodyJson, the one rule extraction and
serving share, now treats a body nesting deeper than the limit minus 16
levels as unusable, so its tool stays a recorded view.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(environment): measure data-plane replies before building them

83fcc739 bounded one /agentenv response to 64 MiB, but it still
serialized each reply whole before measuring it, so a batch of data/get
calls on a large state built every refused reply in full only to drop
it. Each reply is now measured in bounded JSON parts (the shared
jsonParts encoder), its parts kept only while it fits; a reply past the
budget is counted for its exact reply_bytes but never assembled. A test
checks that a refused read is never handed to JSON.stringify whole and
that its reply_bytes is exact.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(environment): release batch replies as they are encoded; judge exact numbers by value

answerBatch kept every settled reply in its pending array until the
batch ended, so a batch alternating data/add and data/get held each
loaded state alive; each reply now leaves the queue as it is encoded.

The exact-number policy judged a number by its recorded spelling, so a
state loaded with 1e20 came back from data/get as
100000000000000000000, which data/add refused, breaking the promise
that data/get output loads back unchanged. A number is exact only when
both its recorded spelling and the one serialization writes are safe,
so integers from 2^53 below 1e21 are refused in any spelling; replay
keeps such bodies as recorded text. A domain test checks that every
accepted number is accepted again once written back.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(environment): keep room for refusals and framing in the reply budget

The response budget counted accepted replies only: a budget error that
replaced a reply, and a batch's brackets and commas, were not charged,

commits.subject: fix(adb): normalize absent installer package sentinels (#4073)
commits.body:
fix(adb): normalize absent installer package sentinels (#4073)

* fix(adb): report a null installer declaration as an absent installer

Package Manager prints its String fields by concatenation, so a package
without a recorded installer shows `installerPackageName=null` in
`dumpsys package`. The projection treated only an empty value as absent
and forwarded the text "null" as a present installer identity, which a
consumer cannot tell apart from a package literally named "null" (#3943).
`versionName` is printed the same way and had the same gap.

The parser now maps the empty value and the `null` sentinel of both
String fields to the nullable result's null at the producing boundary;
a reported installer such as com.android.vending is kept unchanged.

Validation: parser unit tests for the sentinel, empty and missing
installer lines and the absent version name, plus a provider-level
regression through the inspect_adb_package operation; three of them fail
on main and pass here. The issue's four CLI controls through
`rea inspect-adb-package` against a stub adb return JSON null for the
sentinel, empty and missing cases and keep com.android.vending. Typecheck,
lint and module boundaries pass.

Closes #3943

* fix(adb): keep the null sentinel handling to the installer field

Review feedback on #4073: a manifest can declare the literal string
"null" as android:versionName, and dumpsys prints it exactly like an
absent value, so mapping versionName to null would turn a real version
into absence. Only installerPackageName, where no package can carry that
name, treats the printed null as the absent installer. The test for the
version name now pins the retained text.

* test(adb): establish permission inventory in null-installer fixture

Main now reports partial coverage when the requested-permission
inventory is not established (9534e42ec). Give the null-installer
fixture a requested permissions section so it still checks a
complete projection.

fix(source): retain CommonJS requires spelled as exact no-substitution templates (#4511)

* fix(source): retain CommonJS requires spelled as exact no-substitution templates

Admit expression-free template arguments at the CommonJS require gate and
read their single cooked quasi through the shared exact-literal reader.
Scope is the require path only: static ESM template declarations keep their
parse failures and dynamic import() keeps the explicit unknown/partial
<dynamic-import> relationship with no invented target.

Refs: #4382

* fix(source): admit TypeScript-wrapped exact require arguments via the shared literal reader

Address review: the require gate matched the outer AST node, so
runtime-transparent TS wrappers (as const, !, satisfies) around exact
strings or expression-free templates were still silently omitted even
though readExactJavaScriptLiteral unwraps them. Remove the gate and let
the shared exact-literal reader own argument exactness; computed
arguments remain silent and dynamic import() behavior is unchanged.

Refs: #4382

commits.subject: fix(process): report the effective regex heap and uncertain signal retry (#6099)
commits.body:
fix(process): report the effective regex heap and uncertain signal retry (#6099)

* fix(process): report the effective regex worker heap

Node gives --max-old-space-size, including NODE_OPTIONS, precedence over
the worker's 128 MiB resourceLimits request. Name that effective
old-generation heap and stop saying the request has no runtime override.
The matching deadline stays a fixed cap.

Co-authored-by: morluto <morluto@users.noreply.github.com>

* fix(process): keep SIGXCPU and SIGXFSZ retries uncertain

The signal does not prove the retained rlimit was exhausted, so an
unchanged retry may succeed. Project that retry as possible instead of
saying it fails the same way.

Co-authored-by: morluto <morluto@users.noreply.github.com>

* fix(process): leave percentage heap overrides unestablished

--max-old-space-size-percentage takes precedence over the absolute flag
in either order. Node computes that MiB from startup memory, which a
later read does not recover, so the effective heap stays unknown instead
of the 128 MiB request or an absolute flag.

Co-authored-by: morluto <morluto@users.noreply.github.com>

* fix(process): read launch NODE_OPTIONS, not process.env

A preload can rewrite process.env.NODE_OPTIONS after V8 has applied the
original flags, and those flags are not copied into execArgv. Use the
initial environment block when it can be read, and leave the effective
heap unestablished when that provenance cannot be recovered.

Co-authored-by: morluto <morluto@users.noreply.github.com>

* fix(process): leave env-file heap overrides unestablished

--env-file and --env-file-if-exists can supply NODE_OPTIONS when that
variable was absent from the initial environment. The file is not in
/proc/self/environ, so a missing entry is not the 128 MiB request.
An initial NODE_OPTIONS is still parsed, because Node does not let the
file replace it.

Co-authored-by: morluto <morluto@users.noreply.github.com>

* fix(process): leave --max-heap-size old generation unestablished

A positive --max-heap-size or --max_heap_size sets the total heap, not the
old generation, and can stay below the 128 MiB worker request when an
old-space flag is also present. The effective old generation stays
unestablished while that value is in effect. Zero or empty clears it.

Co-authored-by: morluto <morluto@users.noreply.github.com>

* fix(process): leave config-file heap options unestablished

--experimental-config-file and --experimental-default-config-file can
apply a heap percentage from a file that is not launch provenance. The
effective old generation stays unestablished when either flag is present,
including beside an absolute --max-old-space-size.

Co-authored-by: morluto <morluto@users.noreply.github.com>

* fix(process): read launch exec argv from the command line

process.execArgv can be cleared after V8 applies --max-old-space-size.
Linux recovers those tokens from /proc/self/cmdline and leaves the heap
unestablished when that vector cannot be separated from the program entry.
Heap probes compare pinned absolute limits instead of a percentage of host memory.

Co-authored-by: morluto <morluto@users.noreply.github.com>

* fix(process): leave a title-overwritten command line unestablished

process.title and --title replace /proc/self/cmdline with the title.
A buffer without a program entry is not an empty option list, so the
heap stays unknown instead of the 128 MiB request. The command-line
probe does not read /proc off Linux.

Co-authored-by: morluto <morluto@users.noreply.github.com>

commits.subject: fix(process): settle owned cleanup with the launcher's own exit proof (#6205)
commits.body:
fix(process): settle owned cleanup with the launcher's own exit proof (#6205)

* fix(process): settle owned cleanup with the launcher's own exit proof

When owned process-group verification fails while the supervised
launcher is still mid-exit, the supervisor now waits up to the kill grace
for its own child-exit observation and verifies once more after it
arrives. Verification is not repeated when the exit was already observed
before cleanup started, so there is no new evidence and the original
failure is kept. Nothing is signaled based on the wait.

Fixes #6134

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* test(process): bound Hopper session cleanup attempts by exit evidence

The fake Hopper launcher exits after its shutdown acknowledgement. When
the supervisor first observes that exit during a failed verification, it
verifies once more, so the first close makes one or two attempts depending
on timing. The test now asserts that bound. Later session retries, made
after the exit was already observed, make exactly one attempt each.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: fix(ghidra): retry retained language catalog closes before admission (#6210)
commits.body:
fix(ghidra): retry retained language catalog closes before admission (#6210)

The language catalog kept failed .ldefs closes in a module-global set that
only a later catalog read retried, and the provider returned a cleanup error
bound to no owner. Registry admission retries provider close before profile
resolution, so the retained handle was never retried and the original error
stayed incomplete forever.

Read definitions through the provider's caller-owned inspection scope with the
shared regular-file owner used by the seed and extension readers. A failed
close is retained as an exact lease in that scope, provider close and the next
catalog admission retry it, and the translated error is bound to the lease so
confirmed release reopens the same registry.

Fixes #6133

Summary delivery with --evidence_output wrote the bundle, then let the

during staging cleanup after commit returned typed cancellation without
the receipt, and a persistent staging cleanup failure after commit was
rewrapped as a provider cleanup error that dropped published_path.

used. Post-commit cancellation keeps {path, bytes} under

commits.subject: feat(artifacts): make ASAR header admission configurable (#6209)
commits.body:
feat(artifacts): make ASAR header admission configurable (#6209)

* feat(artifacts): make ASAR header admission configurable

ASAR header/index admission was a fixed 16 MiB with no override, so
operators with large Electron indexes could only extract the archive.

REA_ASAR_MAX_HEADER_BYTES now sets it (default 16777216, maximum
268435456). One owner resolves the effective admission for the
classification probe, inventory, ASAR reader and Electron file scope,
including the Electron header cache budget. Startup and doctor validate
the setting; admission refuses an invalid value instead of falling back.
Recovery and error details name the effective value and its source.

Fixes #6176

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(artifacts): resolve ASAR header admission from the caller's environment

The admission read process.env, so composition roots that select their own
environment (createDirectAnalysis, createServer, CLI, optional observation
factories) could not raise or lower it, and an ambient value leaked into
callers that left it unset.

Nothing reads process.env now. ArtifactProvider and extraction resolve the
admission from their environment; JavaScript analysis parses it from the
environment its server or CLI caller passes and refuses an invalid value;
the Electron and V8 providers receive it from their factories. Inventory,
nested ASAR readers, classification probes and Electron page authorization
carry that one value. A header cached by Electron under a larger admission
is refused for a smaller one.

commits.subject: fix(process): record withheld unrelated Linux processes as unverified (#6220)
commits.body:
fix(process): record withheld unrelated Linux processes as unverified (#6220)

* fix(process): record withheld unrelated Linux processes as unverified

The token sweep after an owned command (for example the Ghidra Java probe
run by setup and doctor) failed cleanup when an unrelated same-UID process
started during the sweep and Linux denied its /proc/<pid>/environ. Setgid or
setuid programs (mismatched real/saved IDs) and non-dumpable processes are
withheld by the kernel exactly like another account's processes, which were
already recorded as unverified.

Derive the kernel restriction from the same stat-bracketed procfs read that
already supplies the effective UID: all Uid/Gid IDs from status, and the
root ownership procfs reports for a non-dumpable process's environ. Keep that
fact through exit settlement. Related candidates still fail closed.

Fixes #6204

fix(pcap): report workspace allocation failures by their system cause (#6229)

* fix(pcap): report workspace allocation failures by their system cause

Pcap workspace allocation and snapshot writes mapped every filesystem
error, including ENOTDIR and EACCES from mkdtemp, to a file-size resource
constraint with null limits and worker file-size advice. Flutter's owned
snapshot storage had the same errno-blind mapping, while TShark and sigrok
carried duplicate copies of the correct split.

Move the private-workspace failure projection into one shared owner:
ENOSPC/EDQUOT/EFBIG stay file-size resource constraints with their system
code and path; descriptor exhaustion and every other failure become
provider workspace failures carrying stage, workspace path, failing path,
system code and cause-specific recovery.

* fix(flutter): locate owned storage failures by their workspace

mapOwnedIoFailure always passed a null workspace path, so a descriptor
write or read failure without its own errno path lost every location.
Thread the owned root through: allocation keeps null (no workspace yet),
snapshot failures use the allocated root, and package-reader system
errors propagate to the request owner, which maps them against the
snapshot root instead of mapping early without it.

commits.body:
fix(capture): report scenario path search denial as access denied (#6244)

Electron and process scenario path admission caught every realpath or
stat failure as an invalid_value input issue, so a correct path beneath a
directory without search permission returned invalid_request with
schema-correction recovery instead of a host access denial.

Admission now classifies EACCES/EPERM from path resolution and metadata
reads as the existing AnalysisAccessDeniedError (selected path,
system_code, filesystem-read boundary). Missing, looping or otherwise
unresolvable paths and reachable files without execute permission keep
their input-error semantics. Electron reports invalid selections before a
denial on another field. Process PATH search still continues past a

commits.body:
feat(diagnostics): report a byte entropy profile for one local file (#2331)

* feat(diagnostics): report a byte entropy profile for one local file

The diff adds the MCP tool inspect_byte_entropy and the CLI command
inspect-byte-entropy, both implemented by ByteEntropyService. One
absolute regular file is read offline into observed Evidence: file-wide
SHA-256 and Shannon entropy, then fixed blocks and adjacent runs for an
optional window, using a power-of-two block size from 256 to 65536
(default 4096), with high at 7.2 or above and low at 1.0 or below. A
window past EOF, a missing path, or a non-file is an input error; a size
or identity change during the read is an artifact-changed error; empty
input reports entropy 0; cancellation is honored before and during the
read. Summary detail retains the complete series and returns file
entropy, counts, and the ten longest runs for inspect_analysis_view,
while the registered effect remains read-only Evidence and the
diagnostics docs record the operation and its errors.

* fix(diagnostics): flag zero-size files as not shown empty

Generated files such as Linux /proc entries report size 0 while holding
content, so inspect_byte_entropy read nothing and returned an empty-looking
report. A file that reports size 0 now carries a limitation that the result
does not show the file is empty. The result stays a success because the
tool reads the declared size, which the file-stability checks depend on.

under pwntools-elf in the generated product catalog, because the
pwntools group took every binary diagnostics tool except
inspect_pe_resources. The service reports provider byte-entropy.

it in ByteEntropyService, give it its own catalog group, and name the
pwntools tools (inspect_binary_layout, inspect_recorded_crash)

commits.body:
fix(nativeaot): preserve COPY bytes when hydration output grows (#6254)

The DEHYDRATED_DATA COPY writer evaluated the output buffer before the
reservation that could replace it, so a COPY that grew the hydration
buffer wrote its payload into the superseded buffer. The overlay kept the
advanced length and hashed uninitialized bytes while the report claimed
complete recovery.

Reservation now returns a view of the retained buffer, and every writer
(COPY, zero fill, relative and absolute fixups) writes only through that
view, so no caller can hold a stale buffer across growth.

commits.body:
fix(ci): make Windows PowerShell observers cheap and cold-start tolerant (#6279)

The private-runtime ACL observer spent most of its time in PowerShell
machinery: Get-Acl module autoload, an Update-TypeData guard that updates the
session type table, and a Where-Object/ConvertTo-Json pipeline. On starved
hosted runners this pushed it past the 15s deadline, and one run never reached
the first script statement within 15s.

Read the descriptor through DirectorySecurity with SID-typed GetOwner and
GetAccessRules, check every compared identity is a SecurityIdentifier, keep
Get-Acl/Access/NTAccount/Translate out of the observer with a static check, and
build the JSON by string. Route the snapshot digest, readonly-children and
sharing-reader observers through the same cmdlet-free helper. Record process
uptime at script start, and give observers a 60s deadline that bounds a hung
child while covering cold powershell.exe start. Asserted facts are unchanged.

Electron's utilityProcess.fork(modulePath[, args][, options]) treats a
non-array object in the second argument as the options and ignores the
third. The static extractor only read the third argument, so
`fork("./worker.js", { serviceName })` lost the declared name while
reporting exact, complete coverage, and an object in the second slot let
an ignored third argument supply the name.

Move the optional-argv options selection that child_process already used
into the shared expression-shape owner and reuse it for utility
processes. Unproven argv shapes, spreads and identifier options remain
unknown with partial coverage; nullish options or a nullish serviceName
declare no name, matching Electron's runtime checks.

Wrapper substitution keyed contextBridge findings only by the inner
exposure call's range, so every helper invocation replaced the previous
one while unioning its members: the last key survived with every
invocation's members. Substituted members also listed only immediate
object keys, dropping nested paths that direct syntax retains.

Record substituted exposures per site and per world and key, and replace
the site's syntax observation once after traversal. Invocations exposing
one key at one site describe one API covering each alternative object; a
traced invocation whose key, object or world stays unresolved or guarded
keeps the site's own unresolved observation. Enumerate member paths
through resolved objects with the direct syntax depth bound, which also
retains the depth-limit unknown that substitution previously dropped.

feat(pe): inspect Authenticode certificate tables (#4830)

* feat(pe): inspect Authenticode certificate tables

Add inspect_pe_certificates for IMAGE_DIRECTORY_ENTRY_SECURITY
WIN_CERTIFICATE entries and structurally decoded PKCS#7 signer
and X.509 identity fields. The workflow reads a stable PE image
without executing it or verifying signatures, chains, timestamps,
or Authenticode digest coverage.

* fix(pe): bound and validate certificate DER decoding

- Cap decoded DER values with a shared node budget so sibling fan-out
  cannot exhaust memory before the PKCS#7 check
- Require SignedData version, encapContentInfo and a final signerInfos
  SET in RFC 5652 order, and a signature OCTET STRING in each SignerInfo
- Decode OBJECT IDENTIFIER arcs as unbounded base-128 values, including
  a multi-byte first combined arc
- Decode UniversalString names as UTF-32BE and reject invalid values
- Share PE header admission with the resource layout so a section table
  that does not fit SizeOfHeaders is rejected

* docs: list PE certificates in the translated READMEs

* fix(pe): cap OBJECT IDENTIFIER length and arc size

A crafted type-2 certificate with a 262,144-byte contentType OID stalled
decodeOid for about 20 seconds, because one arc kept growing a BigInt
before the signedData check ran. decodeOid now rejects an OID longer than
256 bytes and an arc longer than 32 bytes before decoding it. Certificate
OIDs, including 2.25 UUID arcs, fit under both caps.

* fix(pe): reject truncated certificate tables and PKCS#7

SignedData now requires one SignerInfo with a non-empty signature and a
complete issuerAndSerialNumber. Certificate names share a 64 KiB decoded-byte
budget and are copied once. A security directory that ends in a short
WIN_CERTIFICATE header fails instead of reporting a complete table. The
certificate CLI forwards the caller abort signal into cleanup.

Certificate and signer serial numbers and validity times now count against
the shared decoded-text budget before they are converted, so a crafted
certificate cannot push megabytes of text into the hashed evidence. The
budget error now names certificate text rather than only names.

Restore the CI workflow to match main: the CI_TIMING_TIER input, the
tier-named timing artifacts and their publication conditions, the Windows
typecheck, and the path and snapshot suites in the curated Windows lane.

* fix(pe): require certificate fields and preserve signer key ids

return subjectKeyIdentifier bytes as bounded hex, and advertise an absolute
path in the PE certificate input schema.
