commits.subject: fix(environment): refuse UNC pathname in file:// URI before fileURLToPath (#6272)
commits.body:
fix(environment): refuse UNC pathname in file:// URI before fileURLToPath (#6272)

When a file:// URI contains leading slashes representing a UNC path (such as file:////remote.example.test/share/state.json), Node's fileURLToPath on Windows throws ERR_INVALID_FILE_URL_PATH because it expects a drive letter or Windows UNC format. This was caught and misreported as 'a file:// uri names a local absolute path' instead of the intended 'a file:// uri names a path on this host, not a network share'.

Testing UNC_PATH against url.pathname before calling fileURLToPath ensures that UNC paths are consistently recognized and refused as network shares across platforms.

commits.subject: feat(python): inspect CPython pyc headers and marshal code objects (#4826)
commits.body:
feat(python): inspect CPython pyc headers and marshal code objects (#4826)

* feat(python): inspect CPython pyc headers and marshal code objects

Add inspect_python_pyc / inspect-python-pyc to read one explicit local
CPython 3.7–3.13 .pyc without executing bytecode or recovering source.

* chore(python): drop unused PythonPycHeader export

Knip reported the type as unused after inspect_python_pyc landed.

* fix(python): bound pyc expansion and decode marshal like CPython

- Count a nested code object reached through TYPE_REF once per copy the
  report carries, against max_objects and max_file_bytes, before counting
  or validating the tree
- Charge long digits to max_string_bytes, reject out-of-range and
  unnormalized digits, build the value in one pass, and report integers
  above 256 bits by bit length only
- Decode TYPE_UNICODE with surrogatepass semantics and reject other
  ill-formed UTF-8
- Map only 3.11 magics 3494-3495 to the py311 layout
- Report non-finite float and complex parts as inf, -inf or nan
- Allow an empty co_filename
- Require bytes for co_linetable and co_exceptiontable
- Bind cleanup-failure errors to their retained descriptor leases

* fix(python): list pyc code objects once instead of a recursive tree

Report each distinct code object once in code_objects, top-level first,
with nested_code as indexes. A child shared through TYPE_REF is no longer
copied per reference, and the MCP output schema is no longer recursive.
Names repeated through TYPE_REF still count against max_file_bytes for
each copy the report carries.

* fix(python): bound shared pyc constants and reject malformed tables

- Cache byte-string digests so a buffer shared through TYPE_REF is
  hashed once instead of on every reference.
- Charge every reported co_consts entry, including tables shared
  through TYPE_REF, against max_objects before summaries are built.
- Resolve the inspect-python-pyc path with absoluteCallerPath so
  link/../file.pyc reads the file the filesystem selects.
- Reject TYPE_NULL inside marshal sequences, as CPython does.
- Reject a co_localspluskinds length that does not match
  co_localsplusnames in the parser and the report schema.

* fix(python): bound shared pyc names and read CPython marshal graphs

Charge each reported code-constant name, keep integer bit lengths on the
decoded value, and list code objects nested inside constant containers.
Accept self-referential lists and dicts, marshal version 0 text floats,
empty code names, the original string byte count, and Python set and dict
lengths. Pass the CLI cancellation signal into command cleanup.

Co-authored-by: morluto <morluto@users.noreply.github.com>

* fix(python): bound pyc key expansion and shared nested code

Charge set and dictionary keys before a shared tuple doubles them, list each
nested code object once per owner, and accept code objects as CPython keys.

Co-authored-by: morluto <morluto@users.noreply.github.com>

* fix(python): correct pyc equality, counts, and nested walks

Summarize code objects only after the marshal graph is complete, and
collect nested code with an iterative walk that shares wrapper results
instead of copying every descendant list. Keep tuple boundaries and the
original string bytes in equality keys, and reject negative CPython counts.

Co-authored-by: morluto <morluto@users.noreply.github.com>

* fix(python): bound shared pyc names and keep the first dict key

Charge every copied name-table entry against the object budget before
building the report array, including empty strings that add no bytes.
When dictionary keys compare equal, keep the first key object and
replace only its value, matching CPython.

Co-authored-by: morluto <morluto@users.noreply.github.com>

* fix(python): walk each pyc dictionary child list once

Keep a container's child array on the nested-code frame so a wide
dictionary is not copied on every step of the synchronous marshal walk.

Co-authored-by: morluto <morluto@users.noreply.github.com>

* fix(python): reuse stored pyc dictionary children when combining

The nested walk keeps each container's child list on its frame.
Combining nested code rebuilt that list, and the 8,000-key regression
still accepted the old per-key copy. Use the stored list, and require
that dictionary to finish well under the copy's runtime while still
reporting a nested code object.

Co-authored-by: morluto <morluto@users.noreply.github.com>

* fix(python): keep distinct pyc code objects and reject corrupt ones

Encode each name table's length and entry boundaries in the equality
key so a different name list cannot share a memo key. Walk tuple and
frozenset keys on an explicit stack so a long TYPE_REF chain does not
overflow. Treat code objects CPython rejects for an odd co_code or an
undersized local table as malformed instead of complete coverage.

Co-authored-by: morluto <morluto@users.noreply.github.com>

commits.body:
fix(wasm): test glue literals for a .wasm suffix in linear time (#6237)

associateWasmGlue tested every glue string literal with
/\.wasm(?:[?#].*)?$/iu. Each .wasm? or .wasm# occurrence scanned to the
next line terminator and failed at $, so a multi-line literal with many
such occurrences took quadratic time on the event loop (about 2.6 s for
192 KB, within the 8 MiB glue limit). Because . cannot cross a line
terminator and $ only matches at the end, test the literal's last line
only; results are unchanged.

fix(wasm): refuse unretained summary delivery before provider work (#5274)

* fix(wasm): refuse unretained summary delivery before provider work

inspect_wasm_artifact with detail summary ran the WASM provider before
checking whether the server retains Evidence. On a fixed server without
session retention a successful provider run was followed by
capability_unavailable, and a failing provider run replaced that
diagnostic with the provider error, hiding the guidance to select
detail complete.

Check retention right after input validation, as the EVM, pcap and
network-capture handlers do, so the refusal precedes any provider work
and keeps its typed diagnostic. Complete delivery is unchanged. The
fixed-server boundary test now injects a vi.fn provider and asserts it
stays idle for refused summaries while complete delivery still runs it.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(wasm): validate caller paths before the summary retention preflight

Review follow-up for #5274. The retention preflight ran ahead of the
semantic input checks, so a relative path, glue path or candidate path
with detail summary on a fixed server returned capability_unavailable
instead of its field-specific invalid_request.

WasmArtifactService now exposes that parse-and-absolute-path step as
validate(); inspect() uses the same method, so the checks stay at the
owning boundary, and the MCP handler validates before deciding on
retention. The composition descriptor and server typing expose validate.

The fixed-server boundary test sends relative path and glue_paths with
detail summary and asserts invalid_request with both issue paths and no
provider call; it failed on 418a66d7d with capability_unavailable.

docs/mcp-contracts.md now claims the before-analysis refusal only for
inspect_artifact, inspect_wasm_artifact, inspect_macho and
decode_interface_builder, which enforce it; inspect_binary_layout and
analyze_javascript_application still analyze first and are left to a
separate change.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* refactor(wasm): inspect validated artifact input without reparsing it

Follow-up for #5274, matching the review outcome on #5288. The MCP
handler validated the request and then called inspect(), which ran the
same validator again, so every call parsed and cloned its input twice.

WasmArtifactService now separates the raw entry point from execution:
inspect() validates raw input once and delegates to the new
inspectValidated(), which runs the inspection for input that validate()
already admitted. The handler validates, runs the retention preflight,
then calls inspectValidated(); the composition descriptor and server
typing expose it. The CLI keeps the raw inspect() entry point; behavior
and diagnostics are unchanged.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(wasm): keep cancellation ahead of raw artifact input validation

Follow-up for #5274, matching the review outcome on #5288. Separating
validate() from inspectValidated() moved the raw inspect() entry point's
validation ahead of its abort check, so a direct call with an
already-aborted signal and malformed input returned AnalysisInputError
instead of the AnalysisCancelledError the pre-change service gave.

The raw entry point now checks the signal before validating, as before,
while inspectValidated() keeps its own guard for the MCP handler path.
A unit test pins the precedence with no provider call.

commits.subject: fix(hopper): bound bridge request frames like the Cutter bridge (#5262)
commits.body:
fix(hopper): bound bridge request frames like the Cutter bridge (#5262)

* fix(hopper): bound bridge request frames like the Cutter bridge

The Hopper bridge read each request with an unbounded readline, so a peer
that never wrote a newline kept Hopper allocating for as long as it kept
writing. The Cutter bridge already refuses a frame above MAX_FRAME_BYTES;
the Hopper bridge had no request ceiling at all.

Read the request line with a 16 MiB bound and refuse a line that fills the
limit without a terminator, using the existing invalid_request diagnostic
before closing the connection. Such a line cannot be answered or
resynchronized, because its remainder would be read as the next request.
The response direction is unchanged, so large decompilation results still
flow, and every dispatchable method carries small bounded parameters.

The stalled-line case keeps its connection open instead of half-closing
it, so the test pins the exact ceiling: a bound one byte larger waits for
a byte the peer never sends and fails instead of passing quietly.

Validation: npm run check:fast (typecheck, lint) passed uncached, and the
new boundary test passed against the real bridge over socket pairs at the
frame limit and above it. Removing only the read bound makes the same test
fail, and widening the bound to one byte past the limit fails it too. The
Hopper boundary and bridge-packaging suites report the same 17 failing
files and 126 failing tests before and after this change on this Windows
host; those failures are POSIX-only probes (Unix socket directories,
os.statvfs) unrelated to this diff. Native macOS Hopper and real-client
traffic were not run.

* fix(bridges): exclude line delimiter from payload limit

commits.subject: fix(hopper): shut down the Linux demo helper orderly so its X lock is removed (#4966)
commits.body:
fix(hopper): shut down the Linux demo helper orderly so its X lock is removed (#4966)

* fix(hopper): shut down the Linux demo helper orderly so its X lock is removed

Teardown SIGKILLed the helper's process group, so run_launch's finally
never ran stop_process on Xvfb and each session orphaned its
/tmp/.X<n>-lock. Later startups count orphans as address_collision.

Ask the helper to stop first: closing its stdin trips OwnerLifetime,
and its finally stops Hopper and Xvfb with SIGTERM, which removes the
lock. Anything still alive after the grace period is reaped by the
token-verified group cleanup.

A helper that already died from a signal keeps exitCode null, so the
orderly-shutdown path treated it as still running and sat out the full
grace period before the group cleanup. Check signalCode alongside
exitCode in both the cleanup guard and the exit wait, and add a
regression test for an already signal-exited helper.

Also hardens the ignored-shutdown test: it now proves the fixture
started (waits for its lock), asserts the helper was reaped by the
group SIGKILL, and bounds the wait by the configured 500 ms grace
instead of a vacuous 30 s ceiling.

commits.subject: fix(setup): tell MSIX Claude Desktop's process view from any private roaming file (#4903)
commits.body:
fix(setup): tell MSIX Claude Desktop's process view from any private roaming file (#4903)

* fix(setup): tell MSIX Claude Desktop's process view from any private roaming file

Some profiles keep writing the real %APPDATA%\Claude, so the MSIX package never gets a private LocalCache\Roaming\Claude folder and setup and uninstall refused Claude Desktop for good. Compare that folder first and, when it has no file, a bounded set of files from the package's other private roaming folders, which the package redirects in the same way. A package with no private roaming file still refuses, now with the manual edit as the remedy.

Fixes #4278

* fix(setup): address review findings on the MSIX roaming probe

Name the configuration setup would write, and both package files for uninstall, in the unknown-view advice. Bound the roaming walk by 1024 inspected entries and a queue no longer than the directories it can still list. Count ENOENT at the AppData path as a direct view only while the private file still exists.

* fix(setup): bound the roaming walk's directory listings by its entry budget

Read at most the names the walk's budget has left, with opendirSync in production, so a crowded package-private folder is never enumerated whole before the budget applies.

* fix(setup): recheck the private probe before accepting a mismatched target

A private file deleted between the two lookups no longer shadows its AppData path, so a redirected view can reach an ordinary copy there. Count a different target, like ENOENT, as a direct view only while the private file still exists.

* fix(setup): repeat the AppData lookup before trusting a rechecked probe

A private file deleted and recreated between the lookups passed the existence recheck on stale evidence. Look the AppData path up again after the recheck: a match with the private target is a redirected view, an agreeing non-match counts as direct, and a probe whose lookups disagree decides nothing.

commits.subject: fix(javascript): drop built-in effects for visibly replaced globals (#4565)
commits.body:
fix(javascript): drop built-in effects for visibly replaced globals (#4565)

The semantic collectors admitted Node timers, fetch, WebSocket, JSON.parse
and global coercions from the identifier spelling alone, so a source that
replaced those globals (`setTimeout = () => null`) still produced resolved
built-in effects. Require the existing isUnmodifiedGlobalReference guard,
which the static analyzer already uses for fetch and WebSocket, before
admitting these effects.

The guard treats any visible possible write as a replacement without
evaluating order or reachability, so computed global writes and guarded
polyfills also remove the resolved effect. The workflow docs now say so.

Fixes #3367

commits.subject: fix(browser): reject empty capture containers beyond the 64-level nesting budget (#3975)
commits.body:
fix(browser): reject empty capture containers beyond the 64-level nesting budget (#3975)

The shared HAR/qlog JSON parser checked depth before pushing a container
using `frames.length > 64`, which admitted a 65th container. Over-deep
scalars were only rejected because literal values ran the same check, so
an empty array or object at level 65 passed while `[0]` at the same level
failed.

Admit a container only while its own level (root = 1) stays within the
budget and drop the literal-value check, so empty and scalar-bearing
containers share one boundary.

Fixes #3960

commits.subject: fix(apple): stop counting single-object NIB connectors as ownerless (#3502)
commits.body:
fix(apple): stop counting single-object NIB connectors as ownerless (#3502)

* fix(apple): stop counting single-object NIB connectors as ownerless

The NIBArchive projection counts every object whose class name contains
"Connector" and has no resolvable NSSource as an ownerless connection
(#2484). AppKit also archives connector classes that annotate one object
and never encode NSSource: tooltips (NSIBHelpConnector), accessibility
attributes (NSNibAXAttributeConnector) and user-defined runtime
attributes (NSIBUserDefinedRuntimeAttributesConnector). Each of them
marked the document's connection coverage partial with
connection_unresolved, raised connection_count, set graph.truncated and
added the "declare no resolvable owner" limitation, although no
connection was dropped. The keyed-archive producer does not treat these
classes as connections.

Skip AppKit connectors that encode no NSSource key. A connector whose
NSSource is encoded but nil or malformed, and every UIKit runtime
connection, is still counted as ownerless.

Across 3924 NIBArchive files shipped with macOS system apps and Xcode,
688 reported this false partial coverage (for example Preview's
PaperKitWindowController.nib, whose only other connector is one outlet);
none do after the change.

* test(apple): keep unusable AppKit connector sources counted as ownerless

Only an absent NSSource marks a single-object annotation. Cover an AppKit outlet connector whose NSSource is nil or a non-reference value, which must still be reported as an unresolved, omitted connection.

* test(apple): split unusable connector source cases into their own block

Keep the connector describe block within the max-lines-per-function limit.

* fix(apple): keep unknown NIB connectors unresolved

* fix(apple): preserve unknown AppKit NIB connectors

* fix(apple): share annotation connector semantics

commits.subject: refactor(pcap): give TShark selection and version admission one owner (#3407)
commits.body:
refactor(pcap): give TShark selection and version admission one owner (#3407)

* refactor(pcap): give TShark selection and version admission one owner

The pcap and packet-capture families wrapped the same caller-supplied
TShark with diverging rules. inspect_pcap_* accepted an absolute
REA_TSHARK_COMMAND or tshark from PATH, while inspect_packet_* and the
server availability policy required an absolute REA_TSHARK_COMMAND and
parsed the version banner with a separate regex.

PcapConfiguration now owns the rule: selectWiresharkTool selects an
absolute environment path or the bare name on PATH and refuses relative
values; locateWiresharkTool resolves a PATH selection to the first
absolute PATH entry holding an executable file; parseWiresharkVersion
admits Wireshark 4.x banners for both providers. TsharkCaptureProvider
and the session availability policy consume these facts instead of
reinterpreting REA_TSHARK_COMMAND, so all four tools accept and refuse
the same configurations. inspect_packet_* still resolves, hashes and
rechecks the located executable, and records selection_source in its
tool Evidence.

Host support and resource bounds are unchanged; unifying them is the
next milestone in #3403.

Refs #3403

* fix(pcap): execute the TShark the shared locator selects

resolvePcapTools still returned bare tool names for PATH selections, so
the operating system could run a tool from a relative PATH entry while
the packet tools skipped that entry and selected a different install.

On POSIX hosts, resolve PATH selections through locateWiresharkTool and
run that absolute executable, failing with the existing tshark_missing or
capinfos_missing code when no absolute PATH entry holds the tool. Both
selections are validated before PATH is consulted, so a relative
environment value still reports its own configuration error. Windows
keeps PATH/PATHEXT resolution in the process launcher.

Refs #3403

* chore: restore main's copies of files the merge hook reformatted

The pre-commit oxlint --fix touched two files this PR does not change; keep them identical to main.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(pcap): share selected tool identity verification

* perf(pcap): retain compact executable identity

* fix(pcap): report missing selected tools clearly

* fix(pcap): read historical capture evidence

* fix(pcap): preserve executable read failures

* test(pcap): cover version refusal and packet-tool availability selection

Address review follow-ups on the shared TShark owner:

- Send a 3.x TShark banner and a non-Wireshark banner through the packet
  provider, pinning the capability-unavailable reason for each and that
  only the version probe ran before refusal.
- Cover the session availability rule for inspect_packet_capture over
  MCP: a PATH-only install and an absolute REA_TSHARK_COMMAND are
  available on Linux, a relative REA_TSHARK_COMMAND is refused even when
  PATH holds TShark, and no absolute PATH entry reports provider_missing.
- Rename the locator test's missing absolute PATH entry so it no longer
  shadows node:path relative.

Refs #3403

* fix(pcap): name the configured path when a selected tool is missing

Resolving the selected executable before launch replaced the runner's
"Cannot run selected tool <path>" refusal with a message that kept the
configured path only in diagnostics, so the public CLI no longer told the
caller which REA_TSHARK_COMMAND or REA_CAPINFOS_COMMAND value to fix and
the pcap CLI boundary test failed. Include the configured command in the
capability-unavailable message and assert it there.

Refs #3403

* test(captures): give the late-cancellation fixture a TShark selection source

The service fixture added on main in 719d56ebf predates the required tool.selection_source field, so its report failed output validation before reaching the late-cancellation path the test covers.

Refs #3403

* fix(pcap): report a probe's pending cleanup when a post-run check fails

When a tool probe returned with its owned process still awaiting cleanup,
a failed post-run executable re-read or identity check threw before run()
reported that cleanup. Probes have no snapshot to carry it, so callers
saw an ordinary error with cleanupIncomplete false while the provider
kept the process and refused the next request.

After the command returns, combine such a failure with the probe's
ProviderCleanupError (cancellation and other command failures keep their
own cleanup outcome). Classify request failures through one
analysisFailure owner shared by run() and executeAdmitted(), and let the
availability probe rethrow any cleanup-incomplete failure instead of
reporting the tool unavailable.

Refs #3403

* fix(pcap): keep a failed executable re-read's cleanup live with the probe's

The combined post-run failure was bound only to the probe's pending
process cleanup. When the executable re-read had also failed to close its
file, the classified failure owned that cleanup, but the combined error's
live cleanupResources omitted the file and could clear cleanupIncomplete
once the process stopped. Bind both the classified failure and the probe
cleanup as dependencies.

Refs #3403

commits.subject: fix(ida): ignore released worker rows when verifying close (#4234)
commits.body:
fix(ida): ignore released worker rows when verifying close (#4234)

* fix(ida): ignore released worker rows when verifying close

Upstream idb_list can observe the owning worker mid-teardown and return a
row whose identity is already cleared - empty session_id, owned false,
is_active false - while input_path still names the private copy. The
post-close check matched that row through its private-input arm and threw
"IDA worker remains registered after close.", failing a run whose analysis
had completed and whose idb_close was already acknowledged, and retaining
the private workspace.

Such a row establishes no live session, so it no longer blocks release. A
genuine peer on the same input keeps a session ID and is still reported,
and the session-ID arm is untouched.

Measured against IDA Pro 9.2 on Windows: 11 of 12 stock runs failed this
way; 6 of 6 passed with this change and retained no workspace.

Refs #3056

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(ida): suppress released rows only for worker backends

The blanked-identity exception reached a gui row as well, and a gui
session belongs to an IDA instance REA does not control, so a same-input
gui binding could stop blocking release. The observed teardown shape
covers workers only, so require backend "worker" before suppressing.

Adds a regression test keeping a blank-identity gui row on the same
private input reported as a blocker, and moves the three blanked-identity
tests into their own describe to stay within the per-block line limit.

Refs #3056

`owned` and `is_active` are strict booleans in databaseListSchema, so

commits.subject: fix(hopper): keep automated Linux setup off non-x86_64 hosts (#3422)
commits.body:
fix(hopper): keep automated Linux setup off non-x86_64 hosts (#3422)

* fix(hopper): keep automated Linux setup off non-x86_64 hosts

Every pinned Linux Hopper package (deb, rpm, Arch) is x86_64-only, but
hopperSetupSupported was derived from os-release alone. Setup therefore
planned and confirmed an amd64 package install on arm64 Ubuntu 24.04 and
the other tested distributions.

Classify installer support with the host architecture where the
distribution is parsed, so setup planning, preflight, installation and
package verification share one decision. Setup now takes its Linux
distribution from the doctor host, as it already does for the macOS
version, and the supported-host remediation text has a single owner.

Fixes #3419

* fix(hopper): install Linux Hopper from the setup host's distribution facts

systemLinuxHopperInstallHost read os-release with process.arch on its own,
while setup planning used the doctor host's injected architecture. Both
agree in production, but a doctor host composed with another architecture
could plan one answer and install with another.

The install host now takes its distribution reader from the caller, and
systemSetupHost passes the doctor host's, so planning, preflight and
installation share one host-fact owner. The unused default host on
installLinuxHopper, the other ambient reader, is removed.

* fix(verify-package): require Hopper readiness only where Linux setup installs it

packageSetupSupport required doctor Hopper readiness on every Linux host
whose host check passed, including installer-untested distributions and,
after the architecture gate, arm64 hosts where setup never provides
Hopper. On Linux, readiness now also requires automated installer
applicability; macOS is unchanged.

This narrows the readiness assertion from #2973 on hosts outside the
installer matrix, such as Kali and ubuntu-24.04-arm.

---------

Co-authored-by: DavidFB-creator <220631175+DavidFB-creator@users.noreply.github.com>
Co-authored-by: Kaoru0822 <208281322+kaoru0822-kitauji@users.noreply.github.com>

commits.subject: fix(setup): offer Hopper installation only where setup can install it (#4642)
commits.body:
fix(setup): offer Hopper installation only where setup can install it (#4642)

* fix(setup): offer Hopper installation only where setup can install it

On a host where automated Hopper installation is ineligible (Windows,
macOS below 12 or with an unknown version, or an unsupported or
unidentified Linux distribution), an unhealthy setup without a Hopper
launcher ended by advising "Rerun with --yes --install-hopper", and the
same run then refused that request. The eligibility rule existed twice
(the discovery proposal and the explicit-install gate, with separate macOS
parsers that disagreed on malformed versions), and the final advice
consulted neither.

Make setup discovery the single owner of Hopper install eligibility. The
explicit gate refuses with the unchanged copy through hopperInstallRefusal,
and the final advice offers --install-hopper only where the host is
eligible; ineligible hosts fall back to doctor remediation. hostRemediation
now checks only the Node.js runtime. An empty or unparseable macOS version
is now refused by the explicit gate instead of installing.

Fixes #3944

commits.subject: fix(lifecycle): retain Android and Kuna descriptors when close fails (#6363)
commits.body:
fix(lifecycle): retain Android and Kuna descriptors when close fails (#6363)

* fix(android): retain snapshot descriptors when close fails

Preserve the stable-file diagnosis or completed copy facts when an APK
or engine snapshot close rejects, and retry that exact owner before
workspace retirement.

Co-authored-by: morluto <morluto@users.noreply.github.com>

* fix(kuna): retain span descriptors when close fails

Preserve completed span text or the short-read diagnostic when close
rejects, and keep session close incomplete until that handle is released.

Co-authored-by: morluto <morluto@users.noreply.github.com>

* fix(android): attribute snapshot cleanup to the descriptor that failed

A finished copy can be nested under another descriptor's rejected close.
Walk that chain, keep the snapshot hash on the partial observation, and
name every descriptor that is still open.

Co-authored-by: morluto <morluto@users.noreply.github.com>

* fix(kuna): gate span admission until a retained close releases

Overlapping requests can pass the entry cleanup check before any lease
exists. Hold each span open through its close so the next open retries
that descriptor instead of admitting another one.

Co-authored-by: morluto <morluto@users.noreply.github.com>

* fix(android): preserve nested snapshot facts when both closes fail

Walk nested close failures so a finished copy and a changed-APK diagnosis
survive when the source descriptor also rejects close. Attribute cleanup to
each descriptor that failed, and classify a nested close cancellation.

Co-authored-by: morluto <morluto@users.noreply.github.com>

* fix(kuna): release recovered span leases before the next open

Serialize span admission and close without holding the queue across the byte
read. Recheck the caller signal after that wait, and drop a recovered lease
from the resource scope as well as the span map.

Co-authored-by: morluto <morluto@users.noreply.github.com>

* fix(android): retain a source descriptor when admission close fails

openRegularFile can reject after the descriptor opens. If that close also
fails, keep the owner on the snapshot cleanup map instead of dropping it
when adoption never runs.

Co-authored-by: morluto <morluto@users.noreply.github.com>

* fix(kuna): keep cancellation when a completed span close fails

Pass the caller signal into span finalization. If the read already finished
and close then rejects, report cancellation as the primary error and keep
the span text with the retained descriptor.

Co-authored-by: morluto <morluto@users.noreply.github.com>

* style: format Android and Kuna close-ownership changes

CI format:check rejected the four files touched by the close-ownership fixes.

Co-authored-by: morluto <morluto@users.noreply.github.com>

* fix(android): keep the snapshot hash inside a nested cancellation

A destination close that succeeds after abort throws RegularFileCancelled
with the finished copy. When the source close then rejects, recover that
copy so cancellation keeps the digest and file-snapshot-hash observation.

Co-authored-by: morluto <morluto@users.noreply.github.com>

fix(mcp): report Linux-only integrations as unsupported_host off their hosts (#5793)

* fix(mcp): report Linux-only integrations as unsupported_host off their hosts

Session discovery folded the host check into each optional integration's
enabled flag, so on macOS or Windows the Linux-only packet, signal,
firmware, pwntools, EVM and Wakaru tools reported provider_missing.
Their execution guards refuse those hosts whatever is configured, so
installing a provider there could never make them available.

configuration and reports unsupported_host with the existing
remediation. Injected services and supported hosts behave as before.

commits.subject: fix(native): admit universal Mach-O files without a host slice (#5501)
commits.body:
fix(native): admit universal Mach-O files without a host slice (#5501)

* fix(native): admit universal Mach-O files without a host slice

FAT Mach-O admission selected only the host's slice and rejected a valid
container whose slices are all foreign, so list-architectures returned
target_unavailable instead of the container's inventory. A thin foreign
image was already admitted.

Prefer the host's slice and otherwise select the first declared supported
slice. Remove the Ghidra installation probe's re-parse under other host
architectures, which existed only to work around the rejection.

Fixes #5404

* fix(native): select the first valid foreign FAT slice

Without a host slice, FAT selection took the first declared slice even when
it was too short for its Mach-O header, rejecting a container whose later
foreign slice is valid. The Ghidra decompiler probe then reported such a
foreign-only decompiler as unknown rather than incompatible. Select the first
foreign slice that can hold its header; a malformed host slice still fails.

* fix(native): select foreign FAT slices from every declaration

Foreign-slice fallback chose among architecture families after keeping only
each family's first declaration, so an undersized first arm64 subtype hid a
valid later arm64 subtype. Select from all declarations, and report the
deduplicated families separately. The host-slice rule is unchanged. Move the
FAT selection tests into their own block.

* fix(native): admit only unambiguous foreign FAT families

With no host slice, a family declared more than once, such as arm64 and
arm64e, has no provider-neutral choice: IDA analyzes the recorded slice while
Hopper prefers its own subtype. Select only families declared exactly once and
keep ambiguous foreign-only containers rejected, as on main.

* fix(ghidra): decide FAT decompiler compatibility from validated families

Slice selection now refuses a foreign-only FAT table that declares one family
more than once, such as arm64 and arm64e, and the decompiler probe reported that
refusal as unknown, so an x64 host accepted an arm64-only decompiler. When
selection fails, read the table's validated CPU families and report the
decompiler incompatible when they exclude the host. Selection and host
exclusion now have separate owners in binaryTarget.ts.

commits.subject: fix(apple): classify keyed-archive objects by declared superclasses (#5228)
commits.body:
fix(apple): classify keyed-archive objects by declared superclasses (#5228)

* fix(apple): classify keyed-archive objects by declared superclasses

Interface Builder keyed archives record each object's superclass chain
in `$classes`, but the decoder classified objects by class-name
substrings alone. UINavigationController, UITabBarController and
UISearchController contain "control" but not "viewcontroller", so they
were reported as controls.

Classify keyed-archive objects by UIKit/AppKit view-controller, control
and view bases in their declared chain first, falling back to the name
heuristic only when the chain names none. The decoder now reads
`$classes` through one helper shared with NSArray detection.

Fixes #5218

* test(apple): cover each declared keyed-archive base with neutral class names

Neutral names classify only through the archived superclass chain, so each
UIKit and AppKit base entry and the control-before-view ordering now has a
case that fails without it.

* perf(apple): parse each keyed-archive class chain once

Objects sharing one class descriptor reparsed and scanned its whole
`$classes` array per object, so 20,000 objects sharing a 20,000-name chain
took about 16 seconds to decode. Cache each descriptor's chain as a set by
archive UID; the same archive decodes in about 3.5 seconds, matching main.

outside 7464 to 268435456 bytes are configuration_invalid.

Part of #6176.

Co-authored-by: morluto <morluto@users.noreply.github.com>

* fix(cutter): keep cleanup ownership when a sent command's reply is oversized

An authenticated command may already have changed the Cutter document
when its reply exceeds the frame ceiling. Return the existing unknown
execution, with the ceiling diagnostic in the message, so receipt
cleanup still waits. A frame that overflows before the command is sent
remains a resource constraint.

Co-authored-by: morluto <morluto@users.noreply.github.com>

* style: format the bridge request ceiling sources

oxfmt --check failed on the five files that set and test
REA_BRIDGE_MAX_REQUEST_BYTES. Formatting only; an oversized Cutter
reply still stays an unknown execution.

Co-authored-by: morluto <morluto@users.noreply.github.com>

* fix(cutter): exclude the LF from the response frame budget

REA_BRIDGE_MAX_REQUEST_BYTES counts payload bytes. The Cutter response
reader and authenticated encoder were reserving one byte for the
terminating LF, so an exact-limit response was rejected. A reply that
exceeds the ceiling after the command was sent still stays an unknown
execution.

Co-authored-by: morluto <morluto@users.noreply.github.com>

* fix(bridge): measure escaped JSON before allocating the request

A command of U+0001 characters can expand sixfold. JSON.stringify of
that expansion can throw past Node's string ceiling before the payload
check. Count the escaped size within REA_BRIDGE_MAX_REQUEST_BYTES
first and refuse it as a resource constraint.

Co-authored-by: morluto <morluto@users.noreply.github.com>

* fix(config): derive the bridge request maximum from JSON expansion

A 256 MiB ceiling still lets a shorter U+0001 command expand past Node's
536870888-character string limit. The maximum is now
floor((536870888 - 296) / 7) = 76695798, the longest such command whose
authenticated frame fits in one string. Requests are still measured
before JSON.stringify.

Co-authored-by: morluto <morluto@users.noreply.github.com>

* fix(bridge): size the Cutter frame deadline and send the measured Hopper payload

The authenticated Cutter command is encoded after the challenge, so a
one-second read rejected an in-budget frame. That read now allows one
second per mebibyte of the ceiling and never waits longer than 25
seconds. Hello stays at one second. Hopper writes the payload it already
measured instead of serializing the same request again.

Co-authored-by: morluto <morluto@users.noreply.github.com>

* fix(config): bound the bridge request maximum by the serialized string

The ceiling already measures escaped JSON, so dividing Node's string limit by the seven-byte expansion rejected encoded payloads that still fit. The maximum is 536870887, one byte under that string ceiling, leaving room for the framing LF.

Co-authored-by: morluto <morluto@users.noreply.github.com>

* fix(hopper): serialize a bridge request when it reaches the wire

The queue kept each encoded frame, plus the caller's params, until Hopper finished the active request. A raised ceiling made a few waiting calls enough to exhaust the heap. The FIFO now keeps the params, and the frame is encoded only for the request being written.

Co-authored-by: morluto <morluto@users.noreply.github.com>

* fix(cutter): hash the bridge proof prefix and payload separately

An exact-limit Cutter frame plus the HMAC prefix exceeds Node's single-string ceiling, so the client threw before sending an admitted command. The prefix and payload are now separate HMAC updates, including the response proof.

Co-authored-by: morluto <morluto@users.noreply.github.com>

* fix(cutter): keep recovery fields when a status path exceeds the frame

A long current_file made the status reply miss the ceiling, and the fallback then dropped session_id and the completion receipts. The status now omits the path and version and still returns the session, connection proof, and up to 64 receipts. That required recovery frame is smaller than the 7464 floor.

Co-authored-by: morluto <morluto@users.noreply.github.com>

* fix(cutter): report an unknown path when status identity does not fit

A bounded status kept the new document generation and omitted the path, so the client filled in the descriptor's older path. The observed path is sent when it fits. When it does not, current_file is null and is not replaced with that stale path.

Co-authored-by: morluto <morluto@users.noreply.github.com>

* fix(cutter): count structured replies by their encoded JSON size

The response guard charged 16 bytes per primitive and two bytes per list slot, so a dense array under the configured ceiling was replaced with output_truncated. Numbers, booleans, null, and container punctuation now use their JSON lengths.

Co-authored-by: morluto <morluto@users.noreply.github.com>

* fix(cutter): stream authenticated responses in bounded chunks

A fitting reply was signed from retained raw bytes, escaped bytes, and a
joined frame, so a ceiling near 512 MiB could exhaust Cutter before send.
Measure and sign JSON pieces, then write the same frame in 64 KiB chunks.

Co-authored-by: morluto <morluto@users.noreply.github.com>

* fix(bridge): keep Cutter admission from stalling or hiding sessions

Read an unauthenticated frame off the accept loop. A command reply that
does not fit keeps completion and generation and reports an oversized path
as null. Discovery reports a ceiling mismatch instead of an absent session.
The maximum HMAC proof is opt-in, and both bridges reject non-ASCII digits.

Co-authored-by: morluto <morluto@users.noreply.github.com>

* fix(cutter): bound frame scans and client response copies

Search only newly read bytes for the framing LF. Unescape each socket
chunk into one response string, check the proof, and then parse it.

Co-authored-by: morluto <morluto@users.noreply.github.com>

* fix(cutter): keep completion, admission, and dense replies bounded

Report completed_connection only through connections that have
terminated. Cap connection threads and keep the listener up if one
fails to start. Batch scalar JSON and fail discovery when any ceiling
mismatches.

Co-authored-by: morluto <morluto@users.noreply.github.com>

* fix(cutter): hash requests in parts and scan escapes once

Update the client-proof prefix and request separately. Stop the response
decoder at the first quote or backslash instead of rescanning the tail.

Co-authored-by: morluto <morluto@users.noreply.github.com>

* fix(cutter): confirm live ceiling mismatches and omitted output

A stale descriptor from a previous ceiling is not a discovery mismatch
until its hello proves a live authenticated bridge. A response discarded
for the frame ceiling after dispatch reports output_truncated.

Co-authored-by: morluto <morluto@users.noreply.github.com>

* test(cutter): close the unauthenticated ceiling-mismatch fixture

The listener that fails the hello proof is destroyed after its challenge
so discovery cleanup does not wait on that socket.

Co-authored-by: morluto <morluto@users.noreply.github.com>

capture-process recorded exit.code 0 for a target a scenario event killed

fix(evm): report the carrier input allowance as a file-size constraint (#6414)

The EVM interface failure translator grouped the stable reader's input
limit with path and format refusals, so a carrier over the fixed 4 MiB
input allowance surfaced as a non-retryable invalid_request whose only
record of the allowance was issue text pointing at the input schema.
The same refusal now returns a non-retryable resource_constraint with
resource file-size and reported_limits.maximum_input_bytes, following
the WABT input translator, while path and format reader refusals stay
input errors. The reply-size write failure keeps its own branch.

Fixes #6053

commits.subject: fix(lifecycle): reject session work once close has started (#6411)
commits.body:
fix(lifecycle): reject session work once close has started (#6411)

* fix(lifecycle): reject session work once close has started

Process shutdown closed the shared binary session without sealing it, so a
stdio tool call could open a provider after that close and leave the child
running. GDB ran a queued console command or a second close after the session
had started closing because the queued turn did not repeat admission checks.

Shutdown now refuses later target acquisition, and a queued GDB command or
duplicate close fails as unavailable once its turn finds the session closing
or gone.

Co-authored-by: morluto <morluto@users.noreply.github.com>

* fix(gdb): block console admission after cleanup starts

commits.subject: fix(apple): report a read-denied selected archive as host access denial (#6479)
commits.body:
fix(apple): report a read-denied selected archive as host access denial (#6479)

* fix(apple): report a read-denied selected archive as host access denial

inspect-keyed-archive reported a host read refusal on the caller-selected bundle entry as artifact_operation_failed/execution_failure with reason io, leaving EACCES or EPERM only inside message text. The caller selected that entry, so the refusal is a selection outcome with its own typed classification, system code and read-access recovery.

DirectoryArtifactReader now marks a refused entry open with DirectoryArtifactEntryAccessDenied, which retains the host system code and the selected entry path. KeyedArchiveReader, which owns the caller's selection, maps it to the shared AnalysisAccessDeniedError, and artifact failure translation keeps that typed error instead of replacing it with a generic io failure. Other readers and other reader failures are unchanged; every existing reason keeps its current projection.

Adds the access_denied projection coverage plus a real host refusal through the production reader and a non-permission control.

* fix(apple): carry cleanup ownership and cover raw refusals for a denied selection

Addresses the two review findings on the denied-selection classification:

- The typed host access denial now carries the reader's cleanup observation, so a denied open that left a resource owned does not project as fully cleaned.
- Adds coverage that starts from raw host EACCES/EPERM/EIO refusals with the real DirectoryArtifactReader open path, so the marker itself is exercised rather than constructed by the test. EIO stays an artifact failure.

commits.subject: fix(sqlite): report result-column capacity refusals as capacity (#6327)
commits.body:
fix(sqlite): report result-column capacity refusals as capacity (#6327)

A projection wider than SQLite's native result-column limit failed with the
generic "too many columns in result set" SQL error. The inspector could not
attribute that error to a generated column, so the worker reported "format"
and the parent blamed the caller's path as invalid_format even though the
selected database was readable.

Classify the refusal from SQLite's own column limit for the private
connection, carry the selected and engine counts through the worker reply,
and project it as a capacity resource constraint. The database stays
readable, no partial rows are returned, and the recovery names the column
counts and splitting the projection across calls.

fix(web): refuse an existing script-export destination as invalid input (#6313)

* fix(web): refuse an existing script-export destination as invalid input

export_web_scripts refused an existing output directory or link correctly,
but reported it as artifact_operation_failed / execution_failure with no
field issue or recovery. SafeOutputTree.create raises that refusal as a
path failure before any output tree exists, and the export mapper wrapped
it as an artifact failure.

Attribute pre-admission path refusals to output_directory as an
AnalysisInputError, as environment export already does for its directory.
Both now share one helper owned beside SafeOutputTree; failures after the
tree is admitted keep their artifact semantics.

Fixes #6029

* fix(artifacts): type SafeOutputTree destination refusals

Admission conversion treated any cleanup-free path failure raised before
admission as a refusal of the selected directory, so an acquired-tree setup
failure, such as being unable to restrict a created root to 0700, blamed
valid output_directory or directory input.

SafeOutputTree.create now raises SafeOutputTreeDestinationRefusal for the
refusals of the selection itself: a relative or reserved root, an existing
root, and an accepted existing root that is not an empty directory. The shared
conversion accepts only that type, directly or wrapped by
SafeOutputTreeCreationFailure, so script and environment export no longer
track admission separately.

* feat(cli): report version and runtime with an explicit output format

`rea --version --json` and `--version --format <format>` ignored the format
and printed only the bare version, so support reports gathered the runtime
and platform by hand.

A root --version request that selects a format now renders a documented
report: package name and version, JavaScript runtime and version, platform,
architecture, and whether the runtime satisfies the supported range. It
contains no paths, environment values, user or host names, and starts no
provider. Plain --version is unchanged, --help keeps precedence, and other
output controls keep Incur's plain version.

The runtime verdict uses a new shared supportsJavaScriptRuntime rule that
rea doctor now uses too, so both judge Bun by its Node.js compatibility
version. mcp doctor's private JSON/format renderer moves to cliOutput as
renderCliDocument and is shared with the version report.

* fix(sqlite): report result-column capacity refusals as capacity (#6327)

A projection wider than SQLite's native result-column limit failed with the
generic "too many columns in result set" SQL error. The inspector could not
attribute that error to a generated column, so the worker reported "format"
and the parent blamed the caller's path as invalid_format even though the
selected database was readable.

Classify the refusal from SQLite's own column limit for the private
connection, carry the selected and engine counts through the worker reply,
and project it as a capacity resource constraint. The database stays
readable, no partial rows are returned, and the recovery names the column
counts and splitting the projection across calls.

field issue or recovery. SafeOutputTree.create raises that refusal as a
path failure before any output tree exists, and the export mapper wrapped
it as an artifact failure.

AnalysisInputError, as environment export already does for its directory.
Both now share one helper owned beside SafeOutputTree; failures after the
tree is admitted keep their artifact semantics.

Admission conversion treated any cleanup-free path failure raised before
admission as a refusal of the selected directory, so an acquired-tree setup
failure, such as being unable to restrict a created root to 0700, blamed
valid output_directory or directory input.

SafeOutputTree.create now raises SafeOutputTreeDestinationRefusal for the
refusals of the selection itself: a relative or reserved root, an existing
root, and an accepted existing root that is not an empty directory. The shared
conversion accepts only that type, directly or wrapped by
SafeOutputTreeCreationFailure, so script and environment export no longer
track admission separately.

feat(cli)!: export row-oriented results as JSON Lines (#5629)

* feat(cli): add JSON Lines output for row-oriented results (#5487)

- Support opt-in JSON Lines format (--format jsonl) for row-oriented results and collection views with clear record boundaries
- Preserve stable source identities and stream records deterministically line-by-line

- Distinguish error outputs with https://rea.dev/schemas/jsonl-error-v1.json
- Reject non-row-oriented results that lack record boundaries with an unreadable_output error
- Document JSON Lines streaming conventions in docs/cli.md
- Add boundary tests covering empty results, multiline strings, partial coverage, large fields, and non-row rejection

* fix(cli): preserve diagnostics, provenance, and nested collections in JSONL

* fix(cli): frame classified failures and reject unrepresented JSONL facets

fix(native): preserve unknown ELF export coverage without a dynsym section

Closes #6792.

ELF images with `PT_DYNAMIC` but no `SHT_DYNSYM` section incorrectly reported a complete, empty export inventory. The shared ELF directory reader now owns the dynamic-segment observation; CLI/MCP report `unsupported` with a reason. Existing symbol-table results remain intact. Read-only format correction; no new execution authority or public schema.

Validation on the current main integration:

- `npm run check`, test discovery, and 166 selected Linux tests pass, including actual CLI/stdio MCP cases and PE/IL2CPP/GPU/Rust reader consumers. Original author validation: 113 tests on macOS, including regressions that failed before the fix; test discovery passed.
- Real Debian libc (1,926,232 bytes) and libLLVM 14 (109,967,296 bytes), with only section-header-count/name-index bytes changed, reproduce the old false absence in both public adapters. The reviewed implementation returns unsupported in both adapters. Independent Python maps unchanged `PT_DYNAMIC` declarations and selected symbol bytes; original `readelf` agrees. The reduced files are not loaded or executed; `readelf -D` itself cannot enumerate these reduced layouts, and that failed oracle attempt is retained.
- Unmodified libc still returns all 3,025 exports, byte-identical complete Evidence and the same Evidence ID as the baseline. Resource-guarded public probes completed without stops or payload leftovers. No speed, memory or model-token improvement is claimed for this coverage fix.

Codex review completed with no findings. CI failed: all 61 observed failures (including 47 omitted from the aggregate report by canceled shards) reproduce with identical complete failure diagnostics on the exact CI base and merge trees. Baseline-only bypass is explicitly authorized for this maintenance session; canceled/skipped coverage remains unverified. See the final CI attribution comment. The original author's readiness declaration below is preserved.

commits.subject: feat(native): export function pseudocode to resumable directories (#6170)
commits.body:
feat(native): export function pseudocode to resumable directories (#6170)

* feat(decompile): write function pseudocode to a directory and return a manifest

Add decompile_all and `rea decompile-all` so a caller can write one
provider pseudocode file per function, or a filtered set, and receive
only a small manifest. The result stays bounded when the program is
larger than a local model's tool-result cap.

Resume continues an export for the same target digest, provider,
analysis profile, and layout. Matching files are skipped, conflicting
files stay unchanged, and one function's failure does not stop the
rest. Cancellation leaves files already written. Requesting dwarf
layout reports that compilation-unit paths are unavailable.

Simulated-provider tests cover the manifest, resume, filters, limits,
cancellation, and the failure cap. MCP registration, CLI coverage,
schema validity, the product catalog, check:fast, and docs:check
passed. Real Ghidra was not exercised.

Refs #6090

* fix(decompile): keep unknown export identity unresumable and recover torn journals

Resume treated two missing target or profile digests as a match, so an
export of one binary could continue into another. Resume now requires both
digests, and a decompiler observation without the export's profile, or with
a different target, is recorded as profile_changed.

A crash during a journal append left a torn final line that made the export
unresumable. Text after the last newline is now treated as uncommitted and
truncated before the next append, and stale temporary files are removed.

An inventory row with an empty address aborted the whole export because its
failure record failed the journal schema. Such rows are now excluded and
counted in the limitations.

A limited resume retried the same recorded failures first and never reached
new functions. Functions not yet attempted now run before retries. File path
reservations come from every journal line, so an output_io record no longer
releases a path. The index is rebuilt from the journal in numeric address
order, and journal close and cleanup failures return a Result.

The cancellation test now cancels after a file is committed and checks that
file survives and is skipped on resume. Redundant snapshot-replay checks are
removed, the CLI limit uses the contract constant, and --snapshot no longer
claims decompile-all updates it.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01AoJZDPcrgmMsCqLG4LfiFb

* fix(decompile): refuse resume of a missing export and repair journals by byte offset

A second review round found that resume against a directory that does not
exist silently started a full new export and reported it as resumed. Resume
now requires an existing export directory.

The torn-line repair measured the committed journal from decoded text, so
damaged UTF-8 could move the truncation point past the end of the file. The
journal is now read as bytes and cut at the last newline byte, and an intact
journal is not truncated, so a concurrent append is kept.

A per-function observation for a different target is now recorded as
target_changed instead of profile_changed. A failure to remove a partly
created output directory is reported instead of hidden. The journal handle is
closed on every path again, including an unexpected throw. The path allocator
no longer gives up after 1,000 collisions and reuses a taken name.

Tests now use createTestTempDirectory, assert journal lines against the
journal schema, and cover resume of a missing directory, resume with an
unknown analysis profile, and a target-mismatched observation.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01AoJZDPcrgmMsCqLG4LfiFb

* fix(decompile): keep a function's first file name across failed retries

Reserving every journal path stopped other addresses from taking a path, but
an address looked up only its latest record. After its file went missing and
a retry failed without a path, the next resume moved the function to a
hash-suffixed name and orphaned the original. Each address now keeps the
first path the journal gave it.

A matched commit still ran the decompiler but did not count toward limit.
The limit now counts every function taken on after skipping verified files.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01AoJZDPcrgmMsCqLG4LfiFb

* fix(decompile): never follow a journal symlink and check procedure_info identity

Torn-line repair truncates the journal, and the journal was opened through
any symlink in the export directory, so repair could truncate a file outside
it. The journal must now be a regular file and is opened without following
symlinks where the platform supports it.

Body ranges from procedure_info were written without checking that the
observation belonged to this export or described the requested function. An
observation with a different provider, profile or target, or another entry
point, now leaves the body unavailable with that reason.

File, journal and index writes now use FileHandle.writeFile, which writes the
whole buffer instead of trusting one write call. The stale temporary sweep is
removed: a matching file name does not prove this export created the file.
The inverted-range test now uses one address space so it reaches the
inversion check.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01AoJZDPcrgmMsCqLG4LfiFb

* fix(decompile): bound returned caveats and keep verified checksums

Ghidra names each terminal call's address in its per-function caveats,
so decompile_all copied one new caveat per function into the returned
Evidence and the answer grew with the program. The returned Evidence
now keeps the eight most often observed distinct per-function caveats,
grouped by provider and text as they are rendered, plus a count of the
rest. Inventory caveats are unchanged, and other workflows are not
bounded. Each function keeps the caveats of the observations it used:
a written file in its header, now including procedure_info caveats,
and a failed attempt in its journal and index record. A procedure_info
observation for another target or profile is foreign and contributes
none.

A failure record for a function that was already written replaced the
record holding its checksum, so after a transient read error a resume
decompiled that function again. The journal now keeps the last
successful write separately from the latest attempt. Resume verifies
against that write and records it again once the file verifies.

A caller abort that arrives while the export finishes now returns
cancellation with the caller's reason instead of a success manifest,
as #6143 does for other late finalization. A publish, index or close
failure stays the primary error.

Also make the missing-journal resume error say what to do, and add
boundary tests: one runs decompile-all through the real CLI against a
fake Kuna to check flag mapping, the relative output directory,
filters and limit; one runs decompile_all through production MCP
registration to check that the caveat bound is applied.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01AoJZDPcrgmMsCqLG4LfiFb

* fix(decompile): keep each function's complete caveats in the index

The returned Evidence keeps eight distinct per-function caveats and
counts the rest, pointing readers at the export. A written function's
file header truncates its caveats after 4,000 characters, and its
journal record kept none, so a large function with many terminal calls
could lose caveats from both the answer and the export.

Every journal record, written or failed, now keeps the complete caveats
of the observations its attempt used, and decompile-index.json carries
them. The header stays a readable summary and, when truncated, says
that the index keeps the complete list.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01AoJZDPcrgmMsCqLG4LfiFb

* fix(decompile): report external functions instead of failing them

Ghidra classifies imports as external functions with an empty body and
returns null pseudocode for them, as its limitations state. decompile_all
recorded each one as an invalid_pseudocode failure ("not text"), so a
dynamically linked program reported every import as a decompiler failure:
34 of 116 functions in /usr/bin/xxd.

procedure_info owns the external classification. When it classifies a
function as external, the export now records status "external", counts it
in counts.external, writes no file and requests no pseudocode. The record
keeps the body fact as observed. The journal header pins the target,
provider and profile, so a resume skips a recorded external function
without asking the provider again; a limit below the external count still
leaves nothing remaining. A null pseudocode result for a function whose
classification is not external is reported as no_pseudocode.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01AoJZDPcrgmMsCqLG4LfiFb

* fix(decompile): report finalization failures after a cancelled export

When the caller's abort stopped the publish loop, decompile_all returned
that cancellation before checking the index write and the journal close,
which had already run. A failure to finalize the export was hidden, so
the caller could not tell the saved index or journal was incomplete.

Publish failures stay primary, then index and close failures. A
cancellation counts as the caller's only when the caller's signal is
aborted, and is then reported after a successful finalization with the
caller's own reason. A provider's own cancellation, without a caller
abort, stays a publish failure like any other. Tests cover an index
failure and a close failure after the caller stops the loop, a stopped
loop with a successful finalization keeping the caller's reason, and a
provider cancellation staying primary over an index failure.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01AoJZDPcrgmMsCqLG4LfiFb

* fix(decompile): remove a created output directory that cannot be secured

createPrivateDirectory ran mkdir and chmod as one step. When mkdir
succeeded and chmod failed, it returned an error before #create reached
its cleanup, leaving an empty directory behind. A fresh export then
refused the existing directory, and a resume refused it for having no
journal, so the caller had to remove it by hand.

mkdir and chmod are now separate. A mkdir failure created nothing, so
nothing is removed. A chmod failure after this call created the
directory removes it with a non-recursive rmdir: it is still empty, so a
path another process filled or replaced meanwhile is refused rather than
deleted, and that refusal is reported.

A filesystem boundary test fails chmod for the new root and checks the
directory is gone and a retry succeeds. A module test confirms that a
function written earlier and now classified as external still reports a
changed file at its path as output_exists.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01AoJZDPcrgmMsCqLG4LfiFb

* refactor(process): share the socket lease with owners other than Hopper

The socket lease that keeps two REA processes from opening the same Hopper
document lived only in HopperLease, with Hopper error messages built in.
A decompile export needs the same guarantee for its output directory.

OwnedLease now holds the lease mechanism unchanged: a listening local
socket that the operating system ends with its process, owner identity
answered by the live holder, and recovery of a stale socket serialized
through a recovery directory. Callers map a tagged LeaseFailure to their
own error. HopperLease keeps its exports and maps each failure to the
same HopperStartError message as before. On Windows the lease is a named
pipe, which needs no stale recovery.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01AoJZDPcrgmMsCqLG4LfiFb

* fix(decompile): hold the output directory per run and stop on repeated write failures

Two runs could resume the same output directory at once. Each read the
journal once, and the index each wrote reflected only its own view, so
the last writer could drop the other run's records. A run's torn-line
repair could also truncate the other run's append.

DecompileExport now holds a lease on the output directory, named by its
device and inode, from before the journal is read (or, for a new export,
from just after the directory is created and before its journal exists)
until the journal is closed. A second run is refused as a retryable
capacity constraint that reports the holder's process ID. The lease ends
with its process, so a crashed run leaves no lock to clear. The lease is
released on every open failure, and a failed release is reported.

An export also kept decompiling every remaining function when its files
had stopped being writable mid-run, for example on a full disk, failing
each one with output_io. After five consecutive functions whose files
could not be written or read, the export now stops with an output error
that carries the counts and the last failures. A verified file or any
other outcome ends a run of failures. Committed files and records stay,
the index is still written, and a later resume continues.

commits.subject: fix(environment): match served items whose route repeats a separator (#6876)
commits.body:
fix(environment): match served items whose route repeats a separator (#6876)

* fix(environment): match served items whose route repeats a separator

callSegments split the tool path template itself and dropped empty literal
segments, while the held collection is split by segmentsOf, which keeps an
internal empty segment. A captured item route such as /api//books/{id} was
stored under collection /api//books but searched with ["api","books"], so
collectionMatch rejected it and a served item read reported the extracted
entity as missing.

Split the call template through segmentsOf, the same owner used for the held
collection path, so a repeated separator is preserved on both sides and the
item answers from its extracted collection. Single-separator routes stay
distinct and param positions are unchanged.

Fixes #6847

* fix(environment): keep repeated-separator collections writable

Preserving empty literal segments in callSegments made createdCollection's
missing-argument guard reject a create whose route repeats a separator, such
as POST /api//books: the empty literal segment tripped the
segments.some(text.length === 0) check and answerCreate refused the valid
route. Restrict the guard to empty supplied parameter segments, so a missing
path argument is still refused while a repeated-separator collection stays
writable as well as readable.

commits.subject: fix(ghidra): report kernel OOM kills as a memory constraint (#6748)
commits.body:
fix(ghidra): report kernel OOM kills as a memory constraint (#6748)

* fix(ghidra): report kernel OOM kills as a memory constraint

A kernel or container OOM killer ends Ghidra with SIGKILL and prints no
java.lang.OutOfMemoryError, so the failure fell through to the generic
execution_failure that points at `rea doctor`.

On Linux with cgroup v2, read the process's own memory.events oom_kill
count before launch and again after a SIGKILL. When it rose, project
resource_constraint (memory) with the group's memory.max, and advise on
the whole process tree (native decompiler processes included) instead of
a larger Java heap. Otherwise name the signal as a possible OOM kill.

Fixes #5859

* fix(ghidra): scope OOM-kill attribution to what the cgroup proves

Review follow-up for the SIGKILL projection:

- The process supervisor records stop_requested before it sends any
  signal, and Ghidra diagnostics carry it, so a SIGKILL from REA's own
  stop is never reported as an outside kill. Only process and protocol
  failures qualify; launcher (start) failures can include REA's rollback.
- Word the memory constraint as an OOM kill in REA's cgroup or a child
  group; the count is per cgroup, not per process tree.
- Keep the open_binary reopen guidance for an established session.
- Resolve the cgroup directory through the cgroup2 mount in
  /proc/self/mountinfo, so subtree mounts are joined from their root,
  and read kernel files to EOF within a budget.
- Report memory_max as "max" for an unlimited group and null only when
  the limit could not be read.

feat(javascript): link assignment right-hand sides to their writes (#6206)

* feat(javascript): link assignment right-hand sides to their writes

A declaration carries its value forward, but a later assignment to a
variable, a property or through a compound operator stopped the forward
trace at the right-hand-side read. The semantic IR now records one
syntactic assignment flow per simple assignment target (ranges, operator,
owning callable), and the graph projection connects each retained read
of the right-hand side to the write occurrence through a defines
relation. Compound assignments also consume the previous value of the
target; the written value itself stays unknown, keeping the boundary of
#4342 intact.

commits.subject: fix(windows): explain when Windows refuses to load the verified native addon (#6832)
commits.body:
fix(windows): explain when Windows refuses to load the verified native addon (#6832)

When Smart App Control or an App Control policy refuses
rea-windows-x64.node, the loader reported the failure as the artifact
stage. Doctor and provider diagnostics then told the user to restore or
rebuild the native files, although their version and SHA-256 had
already matched the package manifest.

The loader now tags a failure of the module load itself, after the
manifest and digest checks pass, as the load stage. The reason keeps the
Windows error text and says that restoring the file cannot help, that
Ghidra and JADX need the native controls, that rea setup can still
register clients, and that REA must run where policy allows the file or
the maintainers can be asked about a signed build. Readiness keeps the
documented runtime_missing code for unloadable artifacts.

Setup does not depend on the native controls: with the addon
unavailable, the published 6.7.0 CLI still planned and applied the
claude_code registration, so no setup gate is changed.

Fixes #5723

fix(setup): preserve cleanup ownership and resource reports (#6920)

* fix(setup): report host-owned cleanup resources alongside the primary's

SetupHost.close documents that it reports the resources a setup host still
owns, but its contract returned only a string. runSetup therefore built the
ProviderCleanupError from the primary failure's cleanupResources alone, so a
resource the host failed to release reached the projection only inside a
free-text reason while the error asks the caller to review the reported local
resources.

Return a SetupCloseReport instead. closeSetupResources absorbs the structured
resources of any cause that reports them, through
ArtifactReaderFailure.cleanupObservation, and leaves opaque failures
message-only so no resource name is invented. runSetup then unions the host's
resources with the primary's before building the typed cleanup error.

Two boundary tests read the close result directly: the skill-cleanup case now
asserts the retained backup path in the report reason rather than in a bare
string, and the shared ownership helper takes an opaque close result because it
only ever awaits undefined from either host it is given.

the new case previously received only the primary resource; 116 tests across
the seven Setup and cleanup-ownership suites pass; tsc --noEmit over the
changed set, its setup callers, and both boundary tests exits 0; oxlint
reports 0 errors; oxfmt --check is clean; verify:module-boundaries passes.
The two failures in src/setupEnvironment.test.ts reproduce identically on
pristine bded9c628 with this change stashed.
