commits.body:
feat(environment): give more write tools a state target (#6385)

* fix(environment): keep read-only POSTs out of the write list

A POST that repeats the latest read of its path, tunnels only read
operations, names a lookup in its path's last meaningful word, or renews
a session no longer counts as a state write: it is replayed, does not cut
initial windows, and does not end observation searches. A tool stays a
write when a related read line changes across one of its calls.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(environment): take an entity an unplanned write made when a read first shows it

A successful item read of an entity the gate's copy never held, after a
write no built plan models, puts the entity into the copy instead of
failing the read, so later writes to it are checked as usual. An entity a
modelled write touched is never taken back.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(environment): plan a create into the type its returned id is read under

A POST whose path names no state type becomes a create into the type
whose item read first names an id its response returned, when the id is
new to the state; serving creates in that read's collection. A successful
POST that returned an id a type's reads only show after it also ends that
type's initial window, so entities a capture created stay out of the
initial state.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(environment): end a type's initial reads at the write its reads disagree across

When a type's reads disagree across a write under another root, the
type's initial window now ends at the earliest write within that change
and the state is extracted again, instead of leaving every view of the
type replayed. The cut composes with the creation cut; the earlier wins.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(environment): replay request lines that show entities in another form

A read line that shows the same entities in another form, by an extra
query parameter that adds or drops members, or conflicts with a base
line on a shared entity, is a variant: it leaves the view's checks and
the entity observations, the view names it with the query keys that pick
it out, and a call matching those keys replays its recording. A filter
role whose name matches no field needs two agreeing values.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* docs(environment): specify and record the state-target changes

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(environment): keep a read-only POST a write when its evidence is incomplete

Body-level container operations are skipped like query ones, a lookup is named only
by the path's last literal segment and never alongside a write word, a tool with a
redirected or unanswered call is not reclassified, and the mutation veto is resolved
over all candidates at once so another read-only call cannot explain a read change.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(environment): answer a field selection only when the state shows it exactly

Serving tests a field selection before any variant key: a projection value a replayed
read gave, or one no checked line gave other than `*`, replays. A list sets aside a
line asking for some fields only before the identity proof, and a dropped variant's
membership change no longer rewrites the type.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(environment): hold adopted entities and linked creates to what the recording shows

An adopted entity is charged against the view's budget like a created one. A linked
create holds only for its exemplar's path arguments: serving refuses others and the
gate counts such a call as unmodelled. A response's identity-named id links at any
length, but a short one only to a type read before the call.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* docs(environment): record the review fixes' measurements

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(environment): release a discarded planning pass before planning again

A rewrite cut clears the first pass, so the budget rewinds to a checkpoint taken after
the write cutoffs and created ids before the state is extracted again. Rewrite spans are
charged and appended without spreading them into an argument list.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(environment): link no create whose id an earlier read showed, and read only whole batches

A linked create is rejected when an earlier list of its type or read of its collection
showed the returned id. Body ids are walked without spreading children into an argument
list. An RPC call reads only when every operations entry names an operation of its own.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(environment): let the gate skip exactly the reads serving replays

Serving's replay decision moves to the domain as replayReason, and the write gate uses it:
a read serving replays can neither approve nor veto a write, and a read of every field
beside a replayed selection is checked. A selection read missing a required field is
still skipped, since part of an entity can neither confirm nor check it.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* docs(environment): record the second review round's checks

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(environment): read writes, links and creation cuts only from evidence that rules out other causes

- A read-only POST repeats only a read that finished before it began; the veto compares
  the latest read finished before a call with the first begun after it, and counts a
  recorded absence on one side as a change. `modify` and `replace` are write words.
- A redirected or unanswered write lets a later item read adopt the entity it may have made.
- A creation cut counts a read still running when the POST began as after it, and a list
  read shows its listed entities' own ids, not those they nest.
- A linked create's item read must come before any other tool's write.
- Line shapes are charged to the budget as they are built.
- A `fields=*` list line is whole, not a field selection.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* docs(environment): record the third review round's checks

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(environment): tie linked creates to their returned ids and order state by the lines left

- A linked create is observed only in a read of an id its response returned,
  envelopes included, and serving takes its recorded path values in either spelling.
- A list read shows a suffix-named identity (`projectId`) distinct across its entities.
- A read-only POST compares the read that finished last before it began.
- An entity's first sighting comes from the lines left after variant lines are dropped.
- The pairwise variant pass stops at a work limit, leaving every line checked.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* docs(environment): record the fourth review round's checks

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(environment): keep foreign keys, stale reads and double decoding out of write evidence

- A list read counts a suffix-named field as its entities' ids only when no
  id-named field identifies them, so an `ownerId` beside `id` cuts no window.
- A read-only POST is compared with the read that finished last among those no
  other write follows, so a consuming call stays a write.
- A linked create's source path values compare as spelled on both sides, so no

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* docs(environment): record the fifth review round's checks

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(environment): compare linked sources by position, decode path fields once and bound read and variant scans

- A linked create's source values compare segment by segment, so a template
  naming two parameters alike cannot accept a changed first one.
- Serving fills a linked create's path fields with its arguments decoded once,
  as the gate learned them.
- The read-only check reads each related line's records once per call, between

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* docs(environment): record the sixth review round's checks

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(environment): replay late and variant-only items, fill linked path fields from the exemplar and charge membership spans

- An item line first recorded after the initial window that names a new shaping
  parameter and shows other members is a replayed variant, like an initial one.
- An item only a replayed line showed, which the state never started with,
  answers with its own recording; one the state held and lost stays missing.
- A linked create fills its path fields from its exemplar's path decoded once,
  whichever accepted spelling the call sends.
- Each membership change span is charged against the budget before it is kept.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* docs(environment): record the seventh review round's checks

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(environment): decide late item lines against the lines left, charge replay keys and bisect rewrite cuts

- Item lines first recorded after the initial reads are decided once variants
  are dropped, against the lines left: a new shaping parameter showing other
  members, or a selection of some fields leaving members out, replays.
- Each replay key is charged against the budget before it is kept.
- A rewrite span's earliest write is found by bisection over the writes.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* docs(environment): record the eighth review round's checks

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(environment): count only reads finished before a linked create began as showing its id held

A list still running when the call began may show what the call made, as the
creation cut already decides, so it no longer refuses the link.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(environment): keep served creates' items missing, check same-type earlier reads, and bound late lines and read-only stretches

- An item only a replayed line showed replays only while no served create has
  added to its type, so a created and deleted item stays missing.
- A linked create's earlier item-read veto checks only reads of the candidate's
  type or collection that show the item, so another type's id does not hide it.
- An item read answered with JSON null shows no id to a creation cut.
- Late lines' member names are charged before they are kept.
- The read-only check precomputes nearest writes and passes once over each
  write-free stretch per path, skipping lines whose reads all agree.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* docs(environment): record the ninth review round's checks

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(environment): link creates past empty item reads, sweep repeated reads once and keep only returned ids for creation cuts

- A linked create passes over a later item read naming its id whose body shows
  no item, such as JSON null, and links the next one.
- Read-only repeated reads are found in one sweep: each path's reads wait by
  end time until a call's start passes them, and a write clears them.
- A creation cut keeps, and charges, only the shown ids some creation returned.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* docs(environment): record the tenth review round's checks

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* perf(environment): compare variant lines through shared entities and parse each compared body once

The variant pass indexes a tool's lines by the entities they show and compares only lines that share one, charging
the index to the budget while it is held; the pairwise work limit still decides when a tool keeps every line checked.
Read-only decisions keep each response body's canonical digest, taken once while its parse is charged, across calls
and veto passes. The creation cut no longer parses reads at or after the write that ends the initial reads, and reads
the ids a body shows inside its lease. Adoption looks up a read's target only after an unplanned write before it.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* docs(environment): record the eleventh review round's checks

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

collection holds none of its ids, so a served item view's reads no longer walk every entity of the type. The variant
pass parses the base lines' queries once for all the variants they key, and not at all when it found none.

rules. Other bug types including 288 stackshots return no crash result.
Opened Mach-O and dSYM UUID joins remain unobserved.

Related to #4297

* fix(apple): keep IPS register literals exact

Use the arm64e fixture integer that matches 0x8527000193ed4944 instead
of an IEEE-754-rounded decimal, and count the lossless JSON example
length from the source text.

* fix(apple): budget IPS parsing and keep typed presence

Parse the IPS metadata and crash body through a projection of the
documented members. Members the report does not interpret are
syntax-checked without being materialized, and thread, frame, image and
the new max_registers budgets run before each row is parsed, so a large
selected file fails with a typed resource error instead of first
expanding every row. Fixed allowances bound JSON nesting, unlisted key
names and termination reasons.

longer read as absence: they are listed in coverage.type_mismatches and
coverage becomes partial, including wrong-type or missing threads and
usedImages collections. osVersion keeps the producer dictionary or the
string form. Frame roles follow physical frame depth, so the top frame
of a non-faulting thread is current_instruction and inlined rows share
the following frame's role. SIGKILL classes compare the canonical hex
once, so 0xdeadd0cc no longer matches dead10cc. Invalid UTF-8 is refused
instead of being replaced, and JSON strings are decoded by copying
unescaped spans.

commits.body:
feat(il2cpp): link generic method instances behind --generic-instances (#5785)

* feat(il2cpp): read generic containers on demand and render method spec names

Generic container indices and records are demand readers on the same metadata snapshot, so links that do not ask for generic instances allocate nothing. Type rendering keeps one graph walk with its workspace, depth and cycle guards; the C#-like names and the Il2CppDumper GetMethodSpecName names are two styles over it.

* feat(il2cpp): link generic method instances with admitted rows and kept issues

generic_instances links every genericMethodTable row through methodSpecs, genericInsts and genericMethodPointers, choosing the one CodeRegistration layout whose counts bound every row. The table is reserved against the report budget before any row is resolved; rows and issues are admitted before retention, and a contradicting row stays unknown with an address-backed issue instead of failing the link. Views page the rows by definition, state, address and name, unrequested and historical collections stay unknown, and Ghidra seeds fold instances after the definitions.

* feat(il2cpp): accept --generic-instances on the CLI and describe it in tool contracts

* docs(il2cpp): describe generic method instances and their limits

* fix(il2cpp): keep issued generic rows unknown and name their row

A method spec that contradicted the metadata still reported its pointer slot as code, while the schema and provider limitation promised unknown. Such rows now keep no address, every issue carries its genericMethodTable row, the domain validator requires unknown exactly on issued rows, and shared specs name one other row instead of all of them. The row-size lower bound moves to the metadata admission owner, the hex helper is shared, and budget wording says checked rather than reserved.

* test(il2cpp): reject ambiguous generic layouts and pin budget, yield and limit paths

* fix(il2cpp): keep unmapped generic slots per row and reject undeclared arguments

Layout selection no longer requires every genericMethodPointers slot to be
mapped; each row reads its own slot, so one unmapped slot leaves only that
row unknown with an issue. Method specs whose class or method argument count
differs from the owner's declared generic container are issued and unnamed.
Fixtures now declare the containers their generic rows fill.

* fix(il2cpp): page generic method issues instead of retaining them in summaries

Summaries keep generic_methods without its issues and count them in
counts.generic_method_issues; the generic_method_issues collection pages
them by rows, indices and fields, as code_gen_modules already does. Docs
also name the method_indices filter the request schema accepts.

* fix(il2cpp): read split generic arguments per slot and method containers on demand

Generic argument arrays may span adjacent loader ranges: admit them with
hasPointerArrayCoverage and read each slot through readPointer, instead of
requiring the whole array in one mapping.

Method generic container indices are read on demand from the method record,
like type containers, so no link path allocates a per-method column. An owner
whose container index is out of range now leaves the method spec unnamed with
an issue instead of naming it unchecked.

* fix(il2cpp): report generic entries past the address space at their row

A damaged methodSpecs or genericMethodPointers pointer could make a spec or
slot address exceed 64 bits. The issue kept that address, which the address
schema rejects, so inspection failed instead of leaving the row unknown.
Check the entry range first and attach the issue to the genericMethodTable
row (or its slot field).

* chore(il2cpp): remove unrelated formatting changes

* fix: restore adb float pattern and mobile fixture from main

The merge commit's lint-staged run rewrote these two main files: oxlint --fix
dropped the escape in [+\-], which is invalid under the RegExp v flag.

* fix(il2cpp): preserve unreadable generic method identities

* docs(il2cpp): record generic-instance workflow verification

commits.subject: fix(ghidra): enforce request limits before encoding (#6917)
commits.body:
fix(ghidra): enforce request limits before encoding (#6917)

* fix(ghidra): enforce the bridge request ceiling before writing

Hopper and Cutter both measure an oversized payload and refuse it before the
request reaches its bridge, using the shared REA_BRIDGE_MAX_REQUEST_BYTES
ceiling. Ghidra had no ceiling on either end: GhidraWire.request wrote the
stringified request straight to the socket, and the Java bridge reads request
lines with an unbounded readLine() after its bounded 64 KiB handshake.

Serialize once, measure the encoded payload, and refuse before the operation
is registered as pending and before any socket write, so an oversized request
never reaches the bridge. Carry the typed constraint as the cause and
re-attribute it in projectPrimarySessionError, so callers see the same
resource constraint Hopper and Cutter already report.

The Ghidra bridge reads no ceiling of its own, so its recovery text names that
only the REA client applies the setting instead of asking for a bridge restart.

Validation: src/ghidra/GhidraClientWire.test.ts (3 cases, red then green),
src/config/bridgeMaxRequestBytes.test.ts (16), src/ghidra/GhidraRequestQueue.test.ts
(25); tsc --noEmit over the changed set exits 0; oxlint reports 0 errors;
oxfmt --check clean; verify:module-boundaries passes. The two failures in the
wider src/config+src/ghidra+src/hopper+src/cutter sweep
(captureDecoderHeap, GhidraAnalysisSeeds symlink EPERM) reproduce identically
on pristine bded9c628 with this change stashed. The Ghidra fixture suite
cannot run on this Windows host: fakeGhidra.mjs renames bridge-endpoint.json
and hits EBUSY on 3 of 3 runs, so the fixture-level test was not added.

* fix(ghidra): preflight request bytes before encoding

commits.body:
feat(environment): serve writes by what their recordings show (#6897)

* fix(environment): keep read-only POSTs out of the write list

A POST that repeats the latest read of its path, tunnels only read
operations, names a lookup in its path's last meaningful word, or renews
a session no longer counts as a state write: it is replayed, does not cut
initial windows, and does not end observation searches. A tool stays a
write when a related read line changes across one of its calls.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(environment): take an entity an unplanned write made when a read first shows it

A successful item read of an entity the gate's copy never held, after a
write no built plan models, puts the entity into the copy instead of
failing the read, so later writes to it are checked as usual. An entity a
modelled write touched is never taken back.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(environment): plan a create into the type its returned id is read under

A POST whose path names no state type becomes a create into the type
whose item read first names an id its response returned, when the id is
new to the state; serving creates in that read's collection. A successful
POST that returned an id a type's reads only show after it also ends that
type's initial window, so entities a capture created stay out of the
initial state.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(environment): end a type's initial reads at the write its reads disagree across

When a type's reads disagree across a write under another root, the
type's initial window now ends at the earliest write within that change
and the state is extracted again, instead of leaving every view of the
type replayed. The cut composes with the creation cut; the earlier wins.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(environment): replay request lines that show entities in another form

A read line that shows the same entities in another form, by an extra
query parameter that adds or drops members, or conflicts with a base
line on a shared entity, is a variant: it leaves the view's checks and
the entity observations, the view names it with the query keys that pick
it out, and a call matching those keys replays its recording. A filter
role whose name matches no field needs two agreeing values.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* docs(environment): specify and record the state-target changes

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(environment): keep a read-only POST a write when its evidence is incomplete

Body-level container operations are skipped like query ones, a lookup is named only
by the path's last literal segment and never alongside a write word, a tool with a
redirected or unanswered call is not reclassified, and the mutation veto is resolved
over all candidates at once so another read-only call cannot explain a read change.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(environment): answer a field selection only when the state shows it exactly

Serving tests a field selection before any variant key: a projection value a replayed
read gave, or one no checked line gave other than `*`, replays. A list sets aside a
line asking for some fields only before the identity proof, and a dropped variant's
membership change no longer rewrites the type.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(environment): hold adopted entities and linked creates to what the recording shows

An adopted entity is charged against the view's budget like a created one. A linked
create holds only for its exemplar's path arguments: serving refuses others and the
gate counts such a call as unmodelled. A response's identity-named id links at any
length, but a short one only to a type read before the call.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* docs(environment): record the review fixes' measurements

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(environment): release a discarded planning pass before planning again

A rewrite cut clears the first pass, so the budget rewinds to a checkpoint taken after
the write cutoffs and created ids before the state is extracted again. Rewrite spans are
charged and appended without spreading them into an argument list.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(environment): link no create whose id an earlier read showed, and read only whole batches

A linked create is rejected when an earlier list of its type or read of its collection
showed the returned id. Body ids are walked without spreading children into an argument
list. An RPC call reads only when every operations entry names an operation of its own.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(environment): let the gate skip exactly the reads serving replays

Serving's replay decision moves to the domain as replayReason, and the write gate uses it:
a read serving replays can neither approve nor veto a write, and a read of every field
beside a replayed selection is checked. A selection read missing a required field is
still skipped, since part of an entity can neither confirm nor check it.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(environment): read writes, links and creation cuts only from evidence that rules out other causes

- A read-only POST repeats only a read that finished before it began; the veto compares
  the latest read finished before a call with the first begun after it, and counts a
  recorded absence on one side as a change. `modify` and `replace` are write words.
- A redirected or unanswered write lets a later item read adopt the entity it may have made.
- A creation cut counts a read still running when the POST began as after it, and a list
  read shows its listed entities' own ids, not those they nest.
- A linked create's item read must come before any other tool's write.
- Line shapes are charged to the budget as they are built.
- A `fields=*` list line is whole, not a field selection.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(environment): tie linked creates to their returned ids and order state by the lines left

- A linked create is observed only in a read of an id its response returned,
  envelopes included, and serving takes its recorded path values in either spelling.
- A list read shows a suffix-named identity (`projectId`) distinct across its entities.
- A read-only POST compares the read that finished last before it began.
- An entity's first sighting comes from the lines left after variant lines are dropped.
- The pairwise variant pass stops at a work limit, leaving every line checked.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* docs(environment): record the fourth review round's checks

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(environment): keep foreign keys, stale reads and double decoding out of write evidence

- A list read counts a suffix-named field as its entities' ids only when no
  id-named field identifies them, so an `ownerId` beside `id` cuts no window.
- A read-only POST is compared with the read that finished last among those no
  other write follows, so a consuming call stays a write.
- A linked create's source path values compare as spelled on both sides, so no
  spelling is decoded twice.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* docs(environment): record the fifth review round's checks

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(environment): compare linked sources by position, decode path fields once and bound read and variant scans

- A linked create's source values compare segment by segment, so a template
  naming two parameters alike cannot accept a changed first one.
- Serving fills a linked create's path fields with its arguments decoded once,
  as the gate learned them.
- The read-only check reads each related line's records once per call, between
  the nearest other writes.
- Member signatures are JSON arrays, so a name holding the separator still
  conflicts; the variant work limit counts line pairs as well as entities.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* docs(environment): record the sixth review round's checks

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(environment): replay late and variant-only items, fill linked path fields from the exemplar and charge membership spans

- An item line first recorded after the initial window that names a new shaping
  parameter and shows other members is a replayed variant, like an initial one.
- An item only a replayed line showed, which the state never started with,
  answers with its own recording; one the state held and lost stays missing.
- A linked create fills its path fields from its exemplar's path decoded once,
  whichever accepted spelling the call sends.
- Each membership change span is charged against the budget before it is kept.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* docs(environment): record the seventh review round's checks

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(environment): blame a failed read on the writes whose fields it disagrees on

A failed item read with no interfering unmodelled write contradicts its creates and
deletes, and an update only when a field the update wrote or its response showed
differs. A create is contradicted when a later read embeds it elsewhere and the state
does not. A create member is fixed to its recorded value when a constant it would
have to change derives from it: its text inside a constant, a referenced entity's name,
or an instant beside a sent date, matched by related field names.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(environment): explain unsent update changes and nested clocks by what the recording shows

An update's unsent change can be a modified-by stamp beside a created-by counterpart, a
value derived from the one sent member stored nowhere (accepted only while the target
holds the recorded before-value), or a sent clock the call left in its own second.
Objects whose clocks all moved with the request are nested clocks, opaque tokens of a
type's own length are generated, and an enveloped body is learned as its one object.
A write takes only its recorded query, an echoed reference to a nested object and a
state word paired with other fields stay at their recorded values, and a slug is tried
before a token.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(environment): order collections by whole lines and sort only arrays a read-back proves sorted

A collection's initial order comes from the first list line that shows every entity its
type's sightings do and applies no order. A view renders a string-array field sorted
only after a counted read-back shows the written values in an order that neither the
written order nor existing-values-first explains, and never once a read showed it
unsorted. Sort and direction parameters share one vocabulary and are never learned as
inert, and a create placed by disagreeing sorts or a random id falls back to last.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(environment): serve bulk writes at a collection and target item actions

A DELETE, PUT or PATCH at a collection, or a POST at its delete path, whose body names
held entities by id is applied to each named entity, and serving refuses it unless every
id is held. A POST to an entity's action path that answers nothing or the entity is an
update of it; it is served only when a recorded call found each scalar it sets already
at that value. Served bulk bodies advertise their items, and compare probes pass them.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(environment): decide late item lines against the lines left, charge replay keys and bisect rewrite cuts

- Item lines first recorded after the initial reads are decided once variants
  are dropped, against the lines left: a new shaping parameter showing other
  members, or a selection of some fields leaving members out, replays.
- Each replay key is charged against the budget before it is kept.
- A rewrite span's earliest write is found by bisection over the writes.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* docs(environment): record the eighth review round's checks

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(environment): set aside response members a path mints anew on every read

A top-level UUID or clock that differs on every repeat of one path's successful reads,
with no write between, is left out of that path's item, list and document comparisons
and named in the view's per_response_members. Serving keeps the recorded value.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(environment): count only reads finished before a linked create began as showing its id held

A list still running when the call began may show what the call made, as the
creation cut already decides, so it no longer refuses the link.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(environment): count a list total nested in a paging object

An item total in a top-level object beside the list, such as pageInfo.totalRows, is a
counter on the same evidence as a top-level one: it must equal the number listed, and
one that differs marks the line partial. Serving and the gate render it from the state
through its JSON pointer and leave the object's other members as recorded.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(environment): take a created entity's nested clocks from its read-back

After a create's generated values pass, its stored nested clocks take the instants the
first later read of the entity shows, as an update's already do, so a create whose
response and read spell the clock differently is confirmed.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(environment): import the compare tool definition as a type

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* docs(environment): describe the new write rules and trim repeated parsing

The environment and capture docs describe sorted arrays, per-response members, nested
counters, item actions, bulk writes, the new write rules and refusals, and their known
limits. `_order` is a direction only. Sorted-array retries and the per-response scan
parse only the reads they need, and identifier words come from one helper.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(environment): confirm no update whose clocks or fields the evidence cannot show it writing

An unsent clock an update left in the second it ran keeps the update unconfirmed until
another call shows the clock stamped. A field the state lacks that the read and the
update's response both show is the update's change, so without a rule for it the read
confirms nothing. A modified-by name stamp brings its id sibling along, and created
entities are indexed by id when a failed read is checked for embeds.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(environment): show pinned query and body values in the served catalog and apply bulk writes atomically

A pinned query parameter is required with its recorded value as the only choice, and a
call that leaves it out takes that value. A fixed body member shows its recorded value,
and an enveloped body its wrapping, in the schema, the description and the refusal.
Bulk writes go through the same query pin and update or remove their entities at once.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* docs(environment): specify and record the write-rule changes

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(environment): keep served creates' items missing, check same-type earlier reads, and bound late lines and read-only stretches

- An item only a replayed line showed replays only while no served create has
  added to its type, so a created and deleted item stays missing.
- A linked create's earlier item-read veto checks only reads of the candidate's
  type or collection that show the item, so another type's id does not hide it.
- An item read answered with JSON null shows no id to a creation cut.
- Late lines' member names are charged before they are kept.
- The read-only check precomputes nearest writes and passes once over each
  write-free stretch per path, skipping lines whose reads all agree.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* docs(environment): record the ninth review round's checks

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(environment): link creates past empty item reads, sweep repeated reads once and keep only returned ids for creation cuts

- A linked create passes over a later item read naming its id whose body shows
  no item, such as JSON null, and links the next one.
- Read-only repeated reads are found in one sweep: each path's reads wait by
  end time until a call's start passes them, and a write clears them.
- A creation cut keeps, and charges, only the shown ids some creation returned.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* docs(environment): record the tenth review round's checks

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(environment): take bulk ids literally, check each recorded call's query once, and keep learned sorts open to contrary reads

Bulk writes take body ids as written, refuse a call naming one entity twice, size updates from the replacements
installed, generate each entity's values from that entity, and delete only with the members their exemplar sent
besides the ids. Comparison translates bulk body ids with the target collection's mapping.

Update rules echo a creation clock sent back unchanged, require every held clock, and refuse a nested clock once any
recorded call kept its object. A recorded call sent with another query than its exemplar's, including item actions,
documents and deletes, neither confirms nor teaches its plan, and only successful calls with that query relax a
create's guards.

A counted read listing a learned array unsorted drops the sort from its view, sort evidence comes only from the
entities the read covers, and a top-level counter whose name starts with a slash is named by its escaped pointer.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* docs(environment): record the review fixes' checks

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* perf(environment): compare variant lines through shared entities and parse each compared body once

The variant pass indexes a tool's lines by the entities they show and compares only lines that share one, charging
the index to the budget while it is held; the pairwise work limit still decides when a tool keeps every line checked.
Read-only decisions keep each response body's canonical digest, taken once while its parse is charged, across calls
and veto passes. The creation cut no longer parses reads at or after the write that ends the initial reads, and reads
the ids a body shows inside its lease. Adoption looks up a read's target only after an unplanned write before it.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* docs(environment): record the eleventh review round's checks

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* perf(environment): list a type's collections only when the path's own holds no id, and parse variant base lines once

The write gate's item target lists the type's held collections, and the removed targets', only when the path's own
collection holds none of its ids, so a served item view's reads no longer walk every entity of the type. The variant
pass parses the base lines' queries once for all the variants they key, and not at all when it found none.

commits.subject: feat(environment): build agent environments from a prompt (#6946)
commits.body:
feat(environment): build agent environments from a prompt (#6946)

* feat(environment): report what an environment serves with an environment-coverage view

A new inspect_analysis_view kind over capture Evidence. It projects the
state an environment derives with the given template rules and reports
each tool as answered from state, replayed with its view reason, a served
write, or a withheld write with its reason, the records behind it and a
hint about what to record next. The hints cover every write reason, so a
new reason without one fails to compile.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(environment): build an environment bundle in one command

rea environment-build <capture> [directory] inspects a HAR (or reads
capture Evidence), projects the environment manifest from the in-memory
Evidence, authenticates the pair, prepares the state and writes the bundle
environment-export writes. Every bundle file is byte-identical to the
three-step path for the same capture and options.

The report adds the capture and manifest identities, the coverage summary,
warnings (a loopback capture named after its file, credential-named body
members by pointer) and the next command. --dry-run writes nothing. The
default template rules are the four the published environments use.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* test(environment): cover environment-build and the coverage view

Domain tests check the hint table against the state view's reasons, the
summary, and the view against the environment-state view it summarizes.
Service tests build the fixture capture and compare every file with the
three-step path, a dry run, loopback naming and the refusals. A CLI test
compares a HAR built in one step with the three CLI steps byte for byte,
and an MCP test projects the view from every source kind.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* test(environment): build the real-agentenv lane's bundle with environment-build

The lane now runs the command users run: it builds the Grafana-shaped HAR
with environment-build and the packed checkout, checks the report, then
runs the bundle with agent-env as before.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* docs(environment): document environment-build and the coverage view

The agent environments guide opens with the one-step build: the report,
the hint for each withheld write reason, and what a bundle ships. The CLI
guide, the capture guide and the skill reference name the command and the
environment-coverage view.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(environment): harden environment-build after review

- The credential scan walks with its own stack, so a deeply nested body
  cannot crash the build, and it also reports credential-named header
  names, query names, form body members and string arrays.
- The build checks SIGINT between stages: cancelled before the bundle
  stage it writes nothing, during the write it names the written bundle.
- A dry run opens the package tarball, so it refuses what a build refuses.
- Repeated template rules are refused, a HAR saved as .json gets a hint,
  file-derived names follow the bundle name rules, `localhost.` counts as
  a loopback origin, and the next command is shell-quoted.
- --capture-timeout-ms passes through to the HAR inspection, and a
  missing directory is refused before inspection.
- The no-observation hint covers updates and deletes of entities the state
  never held; the coverage view states that it does not apply the
  serve-time admission checks; the inspect_analysis_view description
  names the view.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* docs(environment): state the build's conditions and record its verification

The guides now state when the one-step bundle equals the three-step one,
which headers inspection excludes, what the credential warning scans, how
cancellation behaves, and that the coverage view does not apply the
serve-time admission checks. The spec folder records the census, the end
to end runs, the gates and the review.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(environment): dispatch a pending interrupt before each build stage check

The manifest, state and coverage stages run synchronously, so a SIGINT
that arrived during them was only dispatched once the bundle write had
begun. Each check now yields first, so an interrupt before the bundle
stage cancels the build with nothing written.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(browser): send declared requests from a scenario page with a request step

A capture_browser_scenario step `request` sends one declared HTTP request
through the page's own fetch, with its cookies and session, the way the
application's frontend would, and reads the whole response so the capture
records the transaction like any other. The path must resolve to the start
URL's origin, and the page must be on that origin when the step runs.
Query values and header values may be literals or declared secrets, and a
header may read its value from a cookie or a local storage entry, which is
then redacted from later records like a declared secret. `expected_status`
fails the step on any other status. Scenarios without a request step are
unchanged.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* test(browser): verify request steps in a real browser through to a built environment

verify:browser:request records a write session against a fixture item API
that refuses writes without its CSRF cookie header and stored bearer
token. It checks that every request lands in its own step, that the page
values authenticated each write and appear in no record, header or body,
that an unexpected status fails the step and cancels the rest, and that
environment-build serves the recorded create, update and delete.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(environment): export environment bundles over MCP

export_environment_bundle writes the bundle environment-build writes, from
capture Evidence retained in the session or one capture Evidence file,
into an absolute output directory that must not exist and whose parent
must exist, as extract_firmware and export_web_scripts require; it never
creates the parent or reuses a directory. It returns the same report,
whose schema now lives in the domain so the CLI and the tool share it, and
dry_run reports without writing. A loopback capture without a file needs a
name. The build's refusal messages no longer name CLI flags.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(environment): scan scenario credentials, own the dry-run tarball and serialize Evidence once

A browser scenario's retained header values and the query parameters of its recorded URLs are scanned for credential
names as a HAR's are, through a review projection of its records. A dry run admits and releases the package tarball
through the export's regular-file scope, so a close it cannot confirm keeps its owner, and checks for cancellation
after that last await. Evidence is written into one exactly sized buffer instead of chunks joined by a copy.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* docs(environment): record the review round's checks

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* docs(skill): build agent environments from a prompt with request steps and the bundle tool

Add the environments reference to the skill and install it with setup: record
against a disposable instance, sign in through the UI, write with request
steps and read each write back, check coverage, re-record by withheld reason
and export the bundle. Route it from SKILL.md, name agent environments in the
skill description, and document the request step, the export tool and
recording writes.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* refactor(browser): split the request lane and header resolution into smaller functions

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* style(environment): format the build spec

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(environment): say when an untimed capture learns no write clock

Coverage of a capture whose records are not all timed, which includes every
browser scenario capture, now states that the state learns no clock, so an
update stamped with a server-set modification time stays unexplained-change
however often it is recorded.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* docs(skill): give agents a whole scenario shape with step timeouts

Agents guessed the scenario schema field by field and two hung on steps
without timeout_ms. The reference now starts from a complete scenario with a
timeout on every step, and says a scenario capture cannot serve updates the
application stamps with a modification time.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(browser): keep request steps on their origin and their page values redacted

- Follow no redirects: a redirect fails the step and nothing reaches the
  location it names (checked in real Chrome), and check the page's origin
  again in the page as the request is sent.
- Send nothing once the step's time has run out or it was cancelled while
  header values were read; the in-page deadline is what remains of the step's.
- Keep every page value redacted under a repeated or colliding label, keep a
  value's first marker when it is read again, and leave values shorter than
  8 characters unredacted rather than rewriting ids, ports and hosts.
- Refuse a header name given twice, User-Agent (Chrome drops it) and line
  breaks in literal values and prefixes; fail before sending when a secret or
  page value holds them.
- Append query entries after the path's literal query without re-encoding it.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* docs(environment): document request step limits and word bundle refusals for both surfaces

Document redirects, timeouts, page value redaction, HttpOnly cookie sources
and header refusals for request steps. Refusals shared by environment-build
and export_environment_bundle no longer name CLI flags, and the retained
loopback refusal no longer prints an empty file name. The skill reference
asks for read-backs after each write, shows the coverage view's source, names
package_tarball for unreleased builds and the browser path a scenario ships.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(environment): scan every form occurrence and MIME-less scenario bodies

The build's credential scan collapsed form bodies with Object.fromEntries, so a
repeated field kept only its last occurrence: `api_key=secret&api_key=` warned
about nothing although the Evidence ships the value, and repeated values were
undercounted. Form fields are now scanned as ordered name/value pairs, as
headers and query strings already are.

The review projection of a capture_browser_scenario dropped a request body
recorded without a media type, so the scan never saw it. Review keeps such a
body's text with an empty media type; the manifest projection still reads only
bodies it can classify.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(browser): close request step edge cases from the second review

- Append query entries correctly after a path ending in "?", "&" or "#".
- Refuse 3xx expected statuses, which an unfollowed redirect can never
  report, and say a redirected write may already have been applied.
- Redact a page value also as fetch sends it, without surrounding spaces
  and tabs.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* docs(environment): document page value body costs, redirects and MCP dry runs

Document that reading a page value shrinks the bodies a capture keeps under
the default allocation limit, that redirected writes may have landed, that
the MCP dry_run still checks its output directory and which refusals name
the tool, and keep the .har hint in the HAR-as-JSON refusal for both
surfaces.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* docs(environment): record the prompt-to-environment verification

Gates, the real-browser lanes, five environments built from prompts by an
agent on disposable VMs and evaluated with two models, and the two reviews.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* test(skill): count rollback failures from the managed skill files

The environments reference made the skill eight files, so the recovery tests now derive the counts they expect from
MANAGED_SKILL_FILES instead of fixing them at six and seven.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(adb): restore the portable Java float pattern a merge rewrote

A lint autofix during a merge unescaped the hyphens in javaFloatValuePattern, which is invalid in a v-mode character
class, so the advertised start_adb_activity schema failed to compile in every JS regex mode. The file now matches main.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* docs(browser): show the request step inside a whole scenario

Every JSON example in the browser scenario guide is a capture_browser_scenario input the catalog test parses, so the
request step example now sits in a launch scenario instead of standing alone.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(environment): scan structured HAR form params and the request side of unattributed scenario transactions

A HAR request recorded with postData.params and no text is scanned by those parameters, each occurrence counting, and
the review projection keeps the request side of a scenario transaction whose response cannot be attributed, so the
credential warning covers what evidence.json ships in both cases.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(environment): validate build paths and read dry-run tarballs

* fix(environment): report bodies too large for the credential scan

Text bodies over the scan's 4 MiB limit, including a response decoded only as a prefix, are reported as a
credential-scan-incomplete warning by record and side, never by content, so an absent credential-named-members
warning no longer reads as a complete check. The spec and agent-environments guide also state the path validation and
dry-run tarball read that e52ae1cd added.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(verification): release cold source transform services

* fix(javascript): retain capture context along covered mutation paths

* fix(environment): guard request dispatch and report export limits

* fix(environment): admit serialized exports and scan HAR form fallbacks

* fix(environment): admit in-memory build inputs against heap headroom and scan SaveHar null-text forms

The inspected HAR's Evidence and the projected manifest are checked against live heap headroom before they are
serialized, with the same check the file route uses, so a capture too large to parse and seal is refused as
resource_constraint before anything is written. A request whose postData text is SaveHar's null is scanned by its
structured params.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(environment): measure the credential scan limit in UTF-8 bytes

A body counts against the 4 MiB limit by its UTF-8 length, not its UTF-16 code units, so multibyte text over the
limit is reported as unscanned instead of parsed.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(importer): reach package-main selection for trailing-slash directory references (#4219)

* fix(importer): reach package-main selection for trailing-slash directory references

posix.normalize preserves a trailing slash in the specifier, so normalized was sub/ while dirname(match) was sub; the resolvedThroughIndex comparison failed and selectPackageMain never ran for require("./sub/"). Compare against the slash-stripped directory so trailing-slash directory references take the same package-main path as the plain spelling. Boundary rows pair each trailing-slash request with the existing manifest fixtures and are validated against Node's own resolver in the same table.

Fixes #4189

* fix(importer): derive trailing-slash directory identity with path semantics

The lookbehind strip kept a trailing slash when the final component ended in a line terminator (require("./pkg\n/")), so dirname(match) still never matched and the trailing-slash path skipped package-main selection for those directories. Join the normalized path with "." instead: path semantics collapse any trailing slash run regardless of the preceding character, and behave identically to the strip on every other spelling. Boundary fixture gains a newline directory with a package.json, an index and a declared main so the index path (not the no-match branch) exercises the comparison.

Addresses Codex P1 on #4219

fix(ghidra): admit recordless MIPS-I legacy targets (#7014)

* fix(ghidra): admit recordless MIPS-I legacy targets

MIPS-I headers carry a zero-value ISA field (EF_MIPS_ARCH_1) and predate the ABI flags record. The recordless legacy admission only accepted EF_MIPS_ARCH_32 and EF_MIPS_ARCH_32R2, so every MIPS-I target was refused before provider selection even when its ELF32/ET_EXEC shape matched the existing inferred-o32 lane.

Admit MIPS-I through the same recordless legacy path, pin the endian-matched 32-bit MIPS language, and use a distinct support-lane identity so profile-bound snapshots invalidate. Declared-ABI MIPS-I headers remain refused because that lane is verified for MIPS32r2 only. The session reports that the generic 32-bit language also decodes later MIPS32 instructions and that MIPS-I subset conformance is not established from the header.

Fixes #6933.

* fix(ghidra): bind MIPS profiles to their target

Refuse a committed MIPS lane or ELF metadata that was resolved for a different target, including the same-endian MIPS-I and MIPS32 legacy lanes that share a language pin. Report the committed caller-selected MIPS-I language in the session limitation instead of claiming the provider pin.

commits.subject: fix(setup): materialize the pinned package-runner cache before the first client start (#7032)
commits.body:
fix(setup): materialize the pinned package-runner cache before the first client start (#7032)

* fix(setup): materialize the pinned package-runner cache before the first client start

Package runners key their package cache by the requested spec, so the
entry installed for the @latest invocation that ran setup cannot serve
the pinned rea-agents@<version> registration. The first client start
installed that entry inside the client's MCP startup deadline and timed
out (three consecutive 30 s timeouts observed in one client log; a
controlled cold install with every tarball already cached took 22 s).

Setup now materializes the pinned entry once after applying
registrations: best-effort, bounded by a timeout, launched from a
neutral working directory, and non-fatal on failure. The setup result
carries the prewarm summary, interactive output prints a warning when
the step fails, and direct launcher registrations keep skipping it.

Fixes #7027

* fix(setup): gate prewarm to applied registrations and supervise the runner tree

Address review findings on the prewarm step:

- Gate the prewarm on at least one applied client registration
  (configured_<client>), so an empty plan or a skill-only run never
  installs into the package-runner cache; the step now only follows
  registrations the user approved in this transaction.
- Replace execFileOutput with a supervised spawn: on timeout the whole
  runner tree stops through cleanupWindowsProcessTree on Windows and a
  process-group kill on POSIX, because killing only the direct child
  leaves npm holding the inherited output pipes past the deadline.
- Emit started and completed progress events around the prewarm so an
  interactive cold install no longer looks like a frozen setup.

* fix(setup): forward terminal interrupts to the detached prewarm runner

A detached POSIX package-runner group no longer receives the terminal's
Ctrl-C, so setup could exit while the runner kept installing in the
background. The supervised launch now registers SIGINT and SIGTERM
forwarding for the duration of the prewarm: the runner tree is stopped
through the same family cleanup as the timeout, and the default
termination is restored afterwards. An interrupted launch reports a
failure reason instead of a hang.

commits.subject: fix(il2cpp): link arm64 builds whose registrations were inlined (#6989)
commits.body:
fix(il2cpp): link arm64 builds whose registrations were inlined (#6989)

* fix(il2cpp): accept arm64 module arrays loaded through adrp/add pairs

A Unity 2022.3 macOS Master (LTO) arm64 build keeps no static CodeRegistration, so the module-array fallback that only decoded x86-64 RIP-relative references reported code-registration-not-found.
The registration owner now also decodes aligned adrp + add pairs in executable ranges and keeps the same exact-module-set and single-reference rules.
A minimal Mach-O fixture failed on the previous reader (47 passed / 1 failed) and passes here with four fail-closed variants (48/48 binary tests).

* fix(il2cpp): name the matched instruction form in inferred module-array limits

The inferred-array limitation always described RIP-relative LEA/MOV, which is wrong for arm64 results.
The provider now names the adrp/add pair on arm64, and the tool contract and docs cover both forms and state that a located array alone does not finish linking a Master build.
The new arm64 provider case failed before the wording change (1 passed / 1 failed) and both cases pass now.

* fix(il2cpp): accept type tables loaded without a static MetadataRegistration

A Unity 2022.3.62f3 macOS Master build inlines MetadataRegistration as well as CodeRegistration, so linking stopped at metadata-registration-not-found after the module array was found. Registration now infers the only field linking reads, the Il2CppType table, from the one run of type-shaped pointers that covers every referenced type index and whose start is loaded by the existing RIP-relative or adrp/add forms; types_field is null and the Evidence is inferred. The new arm64 and x86-64 fixtures failed on the previous reader (52 passed / 2 failed). Four run-selection variants (interior reference, run extended before the loaded address, two loaded runs, run shorter than the referenced indices) keep metadata-registration-not-found; instruction decoding and record-shape checks are not covered by these fixtures.

* test(il2cpp): pin adrp page deltas, register pairing and type-record shape

Every adrp fixture targeted its own 4 KiB page, so dropping the page delta or its sign extension, the add register check, the type-kind bound or the type-definition bound left all binary tests passing. Fixtures now reach a later and an earlier page, pair an add with a different destination or source register, break the type run with an out-of-range kind or type-definition index, and bound type-table candidates when the metadata references few type indices. Each of those five source mutations now fails 1 to 3 of 85 binary and provider tests.

* refactor(il2cpp): share Il2CppType kind decoding and document type-table bounds

The type-table fallback decoded the Il2CppType kind and class/value-type kinds separately from the type namer; both now use the Types owner. Zero and unaligned words are rejected before mapping lookup (Master sample metadata-registration search 92 to 68 ms). Docs and the limitation state that types_count is an upper bound, that a run spanning mappings or a small referenced type range can fail, and credit Cpp2IL StrippedCodeRegSupport and the data-side MetadataRegistration searches of Il2CppDumper and Cpp2IL. Master sample output is unchanged (11,031 code addresses, 37,025 type rows).

* fix(il2cpp): refuse generic instances when the type table was inferred

An inferred type table has no static MetadataRegistration, so the
genericMethodTable it would anchor cannot be located. Report
generic-methods-unsupported instead of reading from a null field.

* fix(il2cpp): fail closed when an inferred type table is not unique

Adversarial review found that the type-table fallback could pick another
type-shaped pointer table when the real one was unloaded or excluded, could
replace a static MetadataRegistration whose counts matched, and accepted a
run cut short by a mapping end. Require exactly one long-enough run in the
image, ending inside its mapping and loaded by code; skip the fallback when a
record's two counts matched; accept only assigned Il2CppTypeEnum kinds; and
look records up through the indexed file mapping so many mappings cannot
multiply the scan. Docs and limitations now describe the run length as at
least every referenced type index rather than an upper bound.

* fix(il2cpp): keep the type-table fallback cheap and its refusals exact

Review follow-ups: check that an address can lie in a mapping before the
throwing indexed lookup, so words pointing into gaps or zero-fill no longer
build an exception each (64 MiB: 74 s to under 2 s); treat a run starting at
its mapping start like one reaching its end; stop at the second long-enough
run instead of a 64-candidate capacity error; ignore ADRP/ADD pairs on
register 31; and say whether a counted MetadataRegistration was unusable or
no code-loaded run was found. Docs no longer generalize from one build or
state tool history they do not source.

* fix(il2cpp): judge type-table slots by their loaded value

The run scan read stored words, so a dyld-bound slot's placeholder could
decide whether a run qualified. Confirm each slot through readSlot and give
a run bounded by a bound or unresolved slot an unknown extent, so the
placeholder no longer changes the choice.

* docs(il2cpp): keep the failure-reason table layout

Shorten the two changed meanings so the table keeps its column widths and the
diff shows only those rows.

* docs(il2cpp): keep the reason table at its formatted width

* fix(il2cpp): read type-table record fields through the loader too

The previous change confirmed table slots through readSlot but still read
each record's kind and definition index from stored bytes. Read them with
readUInt32 and readSlot, and treat a record field the loader binds or leaves
unresolved like an unresolved slot: the run it bounds has an unknown extent.

* perf(il2cpp): share image mappings across loader-aware reads

feat(environment): explain values an application derives from other fields (#7025)

* feat(environment): explain values an application derives from other fields

Prompt-built environments withheld creates whose responses carry values the
application derives deterministically, which the write model kept as
constants or could not match across calls:

- A composed string is literal text plus parts read from the fields other
  rules write: a field's value, its slug, or a clock's calendar digits. A

commits.subject: fix(browser): admit passive capture events against the shared retained budget (#7043)
commits.body:
fix(browser): admit passive capture events against the shared retained budget (#7043)

Passive page capture retained console entries and websocket frames with no
aggregate ceiling. Every sibling retention surface already enforces
WEB_RUNTIME_LIMITS.retainedEventBytes (8 MiB): the observation session's
pre-arm buffer and document-request identities, the browser runtime sources,
requests, and metadata, the V8 inspector's retained metadata, and this same
capture's script metadata, which has its own count-and-bytes budget. A page
that logs a few hundred megabytes of console text, or sends text frames whose
JSON shapes carry hundreds of thousands of keys, grew the capture without
limit until the process ran out of memory; the MCP response budget runs after
the handler, so the growth happened before any typed refusal could exist.

Admit each console entry and websocket frame against the same shared budget
before retaining it. A refused entry is counted through the completeness
tracker's dropped-events vocabulary, which already carries console_events and
websocket_frames kinds and was so far used only for late scripts, so the
inspection reports a truncated inventory with the dropped count instead of
silently overflowing. Console entry bytes measure the retained representation:
the entry's type, url, argument-type strings, and the text capture's retained
bytes, which the handler already computed per entry. A websocket frame retains
its shape summary rather than the payload, and the shape grows with the
payload's own keys, so the frame is charged the serialized size of the shape
it retains. beginAuthorizedFrame resets the counter together with the rest of
the per-frame state.

Out of scope: response metadata and agent hints, whose rows are fixed-shape
facts already bounded per response, and any new setting. The shared 8 MiB
constant is reused as-is.

Validation: RED then green in src/browser/CdpCaptureEvents.eventBudget.test.ts,
where the console case previously retained every oversized entry and the
websocket case retained the over-budget frame; 26 tests across the neighboring
console, websocket, coverage, and completeness suites pass. On this Windows
host the wider browser project has 26 pre-existing failures in three
Electron/WebBundle worker-spawn files, reproduced identically with this change
stashed (26 failed, 644 passed on the pristine base; 26 failed, 647 passed
with it on the same file set). tsc --noEmit over the changed set exits 0,
oxlint reports 0 errors, oxfmt --check is clean, and verify:module-boundaries
passes. No real browser session was driven on this host; the browser CI lane
owns that coverage.
Each retained entry now carries a conservative fixed overhead, and each captured console text value a wrapper cost, so a stream of minimal entries cannot admit millions of objects into the budget when shapes are disabled; a mixed-kind test locks that console entries and websocket frames spend one shared allowance.

* fix(uninstall): retain unverified shared client configuration

* fix(clients): preserve scoped removal evidence

* fix(doctor): omit undefined selectedClientIds under exactOptionalPropertyTypes

Passing selectedClientIds explicitly as undefined fails typecheck on this
branch (TS2379), which blocks the focused test workflow before any test
can run. Spread the option only when defined.

* fix(update): separate ownership evidence from product applicability

rea update's maintenance scope inspected only product applicability
evidence, so when a FreeBuff profile was absent but REA already owned a
version-pinned row in the shared ~/.agents/mcp.json, the plan omitted
freebuff and left the integration stale. FreeBuff now declares its
registration storage as shared, which proves ownership of an owned row
but never product applicability, and maintenance requests ownership
evidence through that declaration instead of reinterpreting the shared
paths. Doctor and setup keep readiness evidence, foreign rows stay out
of maintenance, and the Doctor exactOptionalPropertyTypes fix makes the
focused test workflow runnable.

* test(dotnet): split oversized operand extent diagnostics describe

The describe callback reached 162 lines (max 150), failing
max-lines-per-function and blocking the pre-push check for this branch.
Move the single-case extent scenarios into their own describe; no test
content or order changes.

* fix(update): preserve ZCode's disabled shared registration during maintenance

The shared user agents file doubles as ZCode's fallback, where
`enable: false` disables the registration. Ownership-based maintenance
read that row as a FreeBuff registration, whose format does not
recognize the flag, so the row was selected and the emitted setup
command rewrote it, dropping the flag and silently re-enabling a
registration the user had disabled.

registrationActivation now honors `enable: false` for any client whose
registration storage is shared, because the activation fact binds every
reader of that storage. Maintenance leaves such rows out; doctor
reports them as stale, matching ZCode's own treatment.

* fix(doctor): let explicit client selection authorize the config read

When an ACL or an inaccessible shared parent made every access probe
fail, a client selected by name was omitted before the configuration
read could return its unreadable-config detail, so doctor reported it
as not detected with installation remediation: an unresolved selected
path collapsed to absence.

An explicit selection now authorizes the read outright and the probes
serve automatic discovery only. A selected client with an unreadable
config reports invalid with the read failure; one with no config
reports missing; automatic discovery still probes before inspecting.

* fix(uninstall): share shared-storage checks between ZCode and FreeBuff

clients() queued ~/.agents/mcp.json twice: once as zcode_fallback and once
as freebuff. ZCode has no discoveryPaths, so its strict read still blocked
uninstall on malformed shared text, despite FreeBuff's new retain-and-continue
behavior. For a valid owned entry, ZCode removed it first, so FreeBuff reported
skipped rather than removed.

Make the shared file's checks and removal one shared decision:
- Add zcodeDiscoveryPaths to ZCode so it has its own applicability evidence.
- Gate zcode_fallback push on applicable, not just zcodeFallbackPath presence.
- Report shared storage ownership as one decision for both clients:
  FreeBuff and ZCode now use clientOwnershipEvidencePaths together, so a
  recognizable REA-owned row proves ownership once for the shared storage, and
  both clients report the same result consistently.

commits.body:
fix(protobuf): exclude trailing whitespace from gRPC-web trailer values (#7069)

RFC 9110 section 5.5 excludes leading and trailing whitespace from a field value. The gRPC-web trailer parser stripped only leading SP/HTAB, so 'grpc-status: 0 ' was reported as '0 '. Trailing SP/HTAB is now excluded too; internal whitespace and the examined byte count are unchanged.

commits.subject: fix(apple): keep the documented terminating process, parent pid and metadata members of IPS reports (#7079)
commits.body:
fix(apple): keep the documented terminating process, parent pid and metadata members of IPS reports (#7079)

Apple's crash report JSON documents termination.byPid, byProc and flags, the body's parentPid, and
the metadata line's build_version and platform. The parser shapes did not list them, so they were
reported only by name in unlisted_keys / unlisted_body_keys and their values were dropped: a
watchdog kill no longer said which process ended it, and process kept parentProc without its pid.
#4297 asks for termination members beyond namespace/code/indicator to be retained as recorded, and
docs/apple-ips.md says documented fields are reproduced.

They are now kept: termination.by_proc, termination.by_pid and termination.flags, process.parent_pid
and metadata.build_version / metadata.platform. The integers are recorded integers, so they count
toward max_integer_text_bytes and a type mismatch is recorded like the other fields.

commits.subject: feat(binary-layout): admit ELF32 i386, ARM and MIPS layout profiles (#7052)
commits.body:
feat(binary-layout): admit ELF32 i386, ARM and MIPS layout profiles (#7052)

* feat(binary-layout): admit ELF32 i386, ARM and MIPS layout profiles

inspect_binary_layout refused every ELF32 object, so router and IoT
firmware (ARM32, MIPS32) got no layout facts at all.

The pwntools adapter now admits EXEC/DYN/REL objects in these profiles:
ELF64 x86-64, ELF32 i386, ELF32 little-endian ARM and ELF32 little- or
big-endian MIPS. Header fields are read in the declared byte order, the
ELF32 header is bounds-checked at 52 bytes, and pwntools' own reported
architecture, class and byte order must match the admitted profile.
Other machines, classes and byte orders keep an unsupported_target
refusal that names the admitted profiles.

The output schema admits exactly those architecture combinations, and
the Evidence subject now names the reported machine instead of always
claiming x86_64.

verify:binary:layout cross-compiles i386, ARM, MIPS and MIPSel
executables and relocatable objects (never executed) and checks every
section name, address, offset and size against GNU readelf through CLI
and MCP. The real-binary-layout workflow installs those toolchains.

Refs #6934

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* ci(binary-layout): install target libc headers for ELF32 fixtures

--no-install-recommends skips the libc6-dev-*-cross packages the cross
compilers only recommend, so the i686 fixture fell back to the host's
/usr/include and failed to find bits/libc-header-start.h. Install the
four target libc development packages explicitly.

Refs #6934

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(binary-layout): size the minimum symbol entry by ELF class

The relocation reference check required a 24-byte Elf64_Sym entry, so
every positive symbol reference in an ELF32 report was refused as
unreadable output. Elf32_Sym is 16 bytes; take the minimum from the
reported class. A 64-bit table with 16-byte entries is still refused.

Refs #6934

fix(javascript): report fork's silent stdio as piped (#7083)

* fix(javascript): report fork's silent stdio as piped

Node's child_process.fork pipes stdin, stdout and stderr when options.silent is truthy and options.stdio is neither a string nor an array, and inherits them otherwise. REA never read silent, so fork("worker.js", { silent: true }) was reported with stdio_mode default (inherited). The unset-stdio case of fork now reads silent: truthy gives pipe, falsy or missing gives default, and an unresolved value gives dynamic.

commits.subject: feat(environment): serve creates whose answers show less than reads, and whole-object updates (#7080)
commits.body:
feat(environment): serve creates whose answers show less than reads, and whole-object updates (#7080)

* feat(environment): take created entities' read-backs and re-derived update members

- A create's observation takes the fields the first read of its entity
  shows that the answer lacks, and an item read's clock spellings, when the
  read agrees with the answer otherwise. The plan records the read
  (observation.read with its shape); an item read then observes rather than
  checks, a list read only adds fields and still checks. Serving merges the
  same recorded objects.
- An update member sent back as the clock the entity held and stored as a
  fresh clock near the call is a clock rule; one stored as the slug of
  another member stored as sent is a slug rule. Both are accepted with any
  value, as whole-object writes send what they read.
